docs.title: COMPASS Documentation
docs.text: COMPASS (Crew Operations Management & Personnel Assignment Support System) is the official platform for STARFLEET International chapter management.

docs.title: Where do you want to start?
docs.text:
• CO Quick Start — New to COMPASS? Get your ship set up.
  • Roster Guide — Add crew, manage transfers, update ranks.
  • Promotions Guide — Submit promotions and track requirements.
  • Events Guide — Log meetings and track attendance.
  • Set Up or Recover Your Account — No welcome email, or forgot your password? Use your db.sfi.org account.

docs.title: What is COMPASS?
docs.text:
COMPASS replaces the legacy Access database with a modern, multi-ship platform giving COs real-time visibility into crew activity and promotion progress. It manages crew rosters, promotions, events, awards, academy records, and announcements.

COMPASS is a supplemental platform — it works alongside the SFI Members Portal (db.sfi.org), not as a replacement.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: Check the relevant guide's Common Issues section, or contact your Regional Coordinator.

docs.title: Commanding Officer Guide
docs.text: This guide covers everything a CO (or XO) needs to run their ship effectively in COMPASS.

docs.title: Your Role in COMPASS
docs.text:
As CO, you are the primary administrator for your ship's data. Your XO shares most permissions and can act on your behalf for all day-to-day operations.

Keep It Current

COMPASS is most useful when data is entered promptly. A roster updated weekly takes about 5 minutes. A roster updated quarterly takes hours to reconcile.

docs.title: Announcements and Social Posting
docs.text:
Announcements are how your command team tells the crew something everyone should see — a meeting change, a contest, the monthly newsletter. An announcement appears on every crew member's dashboard. It can also be posted automatically to your chapter's Discord, Facebook Page and X account at the same moment.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Task Who Post, edit and delete ship announcements CO, XO Set up Discord, Facebook and X channels CO, XO, OPS, SO Read announcements All crew

docs.title: Posting an announcement
docs.text:
1. On the Command Dashboard, find Ship Announcements and click + New. (Or click Manage, then + New Announcement.)

  2. Fill in the form.

    • Title and Body — the body supports bold, italic, underline, lists and links.
    • Priority — Info for general news, Important for things that need attention, Urgent for immediate action. Priority sets the badge colour and how the post looks on Discord and X.
    • Pin this announcement — pinned announcements always appear first.
    • Publish Date — leave blank to publish now, or pick a future date and time.
    • Expiration Date — leave blank to keep it up until you remove it, or pick a date for it to disappear.
    • Cross-Post to External Channels — tick each channel to post to. This section only appears once you've set up a channel.

  3. Click Create Announcement.

Scheduled announcements aren't cross-posted automatically

Cross-posting happens when you click Create Announcement, and only if the announcement is live at that moment. An announcement with a future Publish Date appears on dashboards when its date arrives, but it is not sent to Discord, Facebook or X on its own. When it goes live, open Announcements and use Publish on that row to send it to your channels.

docs.title: Managing announcements
docs.text:
Click Manage under Ship Announcements on the Command Dashboard.

The totals across the top count all, Active, Drafts (scheduled for the future) and Pinned announcements. For each announcement you can see its priority, status (Active, Draft or Expired), author, how many crew have dismissed it, and when it was published and expires.

  • ✏️ Edit — change the text, priority, pin, or dates.
  • 🗑️ Delete — removes it from COMPASS. Posts already on Discord, Facebook or X are not removed; delete those on each platform.
  • Publish — send an announcement to one or more channels after the fact.

docs.title: How crew see announcements
docs.text: Active announcements appear in the Announcements card on every crew member's dashboard, pinned ones first. A crew member can dismiss an announcement to hide it from their own dashboard; the Dismissed By column counts how many have.

docs.title: Setting up channels
docs.text:
Channels connect COMPASS to the places your crew already are. Go to Announcements → ⚡ Channels.

Under Add Channel you'll see the services you can connect. You can set up several of each — for example, two Discord channels.

Note

On compass.sfi.org, Facebook and X show a Connect with… button that signs you in directly, plus a Manual Setup option. The screenshot above, from a test copy, shows Configure for all three.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text:
Discord channels use a webhook — a private address Discord gives you for posting into one channel.

  1. In Discord, open the channel you want announcements in, and click the ⚙️ next to its name.
  2. Go to Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook.
  3. Name it (for example, "COMPASS Announcements") and click Copy Webhook URL.
  4. In COMPASS, click Configure on Discord Webhook.
  5. Give the channel a display name and paste the Webhook URL.
  6. Optionally set a Bot Display Name, and a Mention Role ID for Urgent Alerts — that role is pinged whenever you post an Urgent announcement.
  7. Click Save Channel.

Discord posts use the announcement's priority for the embed colour, and highlight pinned announcements.

docs.title: Facebook Page
docs.text:
You must be an admin of the Facebook Page.

  1. Click Connect with Facebook and sign in to Facebook.
  2. Approve COMPASS.
  3. Choose the Page to post to from the list of Pages you manage.
  4. Check the Display Name and save.

Facebook posts include the announcement's title and text. In the channel's settings you can set Include COMPASS Link to add a link at the end of each post.

Facebook authorization lapses after about 90 days

Facebook stops letting COMPASS post roughly 90 days after you connect, and nothing can renew it automatically. COMPASS checks every day and reminds your officers 30, 15, 7 and 1 day before the deadline. The channel shows Expires in …, then Reconnect needed once it has lapsed.

To renew, someone with a role on the Facebook Page clicks Connect with Facebook again on the Channels page.

docs.title: X (Twitter)
docs.text:
1. Click Connect with X.
  2. You're taken to X. The account you're signed in to on X is the one that gets connected, so check that first.
  3. Approve COMPASS. You're returned to COMPASS, and the channel is set up — there are no keys to copy.

Posts on X are limited to 280 characters. COMPASS posts the title, as much of the body as fits (ending in "…" if it's cut short), and your ship's name. Urgent announcements start with 🔴 URGENT and Important ones with 🟠.

docs.title: Looking after your channels
docs.text:
The Configured Channels list shows each channel's status and how many posts it has made.

  • 🔗 Test Connection — checks that COMPASS can still reach the service.
  • ✏️ Edit — rename it, change its settings, or switch Channel Active off to pause posting without losing the setup.
  • 🗑️ Delete — removes the channel from COMPASS.

A channel can be Active and still unable to post if its authorization has lapsed. Watch for Reconnect needed or Check failed next to the status.

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
I posted an announcement but it didn't appear on Facebook. Check the channel on the Channels page. Reconnect needed means Facebook's authorization lapsed; reconnect it, then use Publish on the announcement to send it again.

I scheduled an announcement and it never reached Discord. That's expected — see the warning above. Use Publish once it's live.

Can crew members reply or comment? Not in COMPASS. Replies and reactions happen on Discord, Facebook or X.

Do regional announcements work the same way? Yes. Your Regional Coordinator posts region-wide announcements from the Regional Dashboard, and they appear on every crew member's dashboard in the region.

docs.title: Awards & Nominations
docs.text:
COMPASS manages the full awards workflow from CO nominations through regional approval and permanent point awards.

Go to Awards in the left navigation.

Approving, presenting, and submitting to SFI

These three are CO abilities, but a CO can delegate any of them to their XO — see Delegating Command Authority. Nominating and giving awards need no grant; the XO can already do both.

docs.title: Nominating a Crew Member
docs.text:
Go to Awards → Nominate (or click Awards & Recognition from the Command Dashboard).

The nomination form requires:

  • Nominee — Search by name or SCC number. Check Nominee is not in COMPASS if nominating a member from outside the platform.
  • Award Type — Filter the award catalog by category (Order of Merit, Annual Awards, Auxiliary Awards, Regional Awards, Ship Awards)
  • Award — Select the specific award from the filtered list
  • Citation — A narrative description of why the crew member deserves this award (minimum 50 characters, up to 3000)
  • Supporting Evidence — Optional additional details, links, or documentation

Write a Good Citation

Be specific. "For organizing three consecutive monthly meetings during the CO's LOA, maintaining 90% crew attendance" is far stronger than "for outstanding service." The RC uses your citation when reviewing the nomination — a vague citation slows approval.

docs.title: After Submitting
docs.text:
Once submitted, your nomination is visible on the Award Nominations page with a status badge.

Nominations move through these statuses:

Status Meaning Pending CO Review Just submitted, awaiting your own review queue (for crew-submitted nominations) In Progress Under regional review Approved Approved — permanent points awarded automatically Rejected Not approved — a reason is provided Approved – ACTION REQUIRED: Email to SFI Order of Merit only. Approved in COMPASS but not yet sent to SFI — see Sending an Order of Merit to SFI Submitted to SFI The form has been emailed; waiting on SFI's decision Awarded by SFI / Rejected by SFI SFI's decision, recorded in COMPASS once it arrives

docs.title: Sending an Order of Merit to SFI
docs.text:
Approving an Order of Merit does not send it to SFI

COMPASS prepares the paperwork, but you send it. Until you email the form and mark it submitted, the nomination sits with you and SFI never sees it.

The moment an Order of Merit is approved, COMPASS stops you with this reminder:

docs.title: The three steps
docs.text:
1. Download the OoM form. Click Download OOM Form (PDF) — in the pop-up, in the reminder banner, or on the nomination page. The form comes pre-filled with the nominee, nominator, chapter, and citation.
  2. Email it to the Merits Director — SFI MemServ - Merits Director at merit@sfi.org, with the PDF attached. The Open email to merit@sfi.org button on the nomination page starts the email with the subject filled in; you still attach the PDF yourself.
  3. Click Mark as Submitted to SFI on the nomination. This is what tells COMPASS the job is done.

The nomination page lays the same steps out at the top of the submission panel:

Mark as Submitted to SFI is at the bottom of that panel, below the reference copy of the form data. COMPASS asks you to confirm you have emailed the form before it records the submission.

docs.title: Until you do, COMPASS keeps reminding you
docs.text:
A banner sits at the top of every page until each nomination is marked submitted. It can't be dismissed. Each row links to the nomination and to its form, and the banner changes colour as the nomination waits: amber at first, orange after 7 days, red after 14.

Your dashboard also shows a red card for them:

On a phone

The banner appears the same way on a phone, above the page content.

docs.title: After you mark it submitted
docs.text: The status changes to Submitted to SFI and the reminders clear. When SFI replies, open the nomination and click Awarded by SFI or Rejected by SFI. Awarded puts the award on the member's record — or holds it for presentation, if the nomination was set to Hold until presented.

docs.title: Who can send it
docs.text: The CO of the nominee's chapter, or the XO if you've delegated submitting to SFI (see Delegating Command Authority). The region's RC, VRC and RAO can also send it and see the same reminders. Whoever sends it should mark it submitted, so it isn't emailed twice.

docs.title: Award Categories
docs.text:
Category Examples Order of Merit SFI's primary award series — multiple classes and grades Annual Awards SFI annual cycle awards (CO of the Year, etc.) Auxiliary Awards SFMC and other auxiliary-specific awards Regional Awards Awards created and managed at the regional level Ship Awards Awards created by your ship's command staff

Each award's point value is applied automatically to the member's permanent points upon approval.

docs.title: Permanent Points
docs.text: Approved awards add to a member's permanent point total, which contributes to promotion eligibility. You can see a member's full permanent points breakdown by going to Permanent Points in the left navigation.

docs.title: Annual Awards
docs.text: The SFI annual award cycle is managed separately from regular nominations. Nominations are submitted during a specific window announced by your RC. EC-level annual awards are voted on by the Executive Committee. Your RC will announce when the window opens — watch for that communication.

docs.title: RC-Level Award Workflow
docs.text: For reference, once you submit a nomination your RC sees it in their regional awards queue for review and approval. The RC can approve directly or request changes.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Award not in the catalog. Contact your RC — the award catalog is managed at the regional and fleet level. Custom ship awards can be added by your RC on request.

Points didn't update after approval. Refresh the member's profile. If still missing, contact the platform admin.

I submitted with the wrong nominee. Contact your RC before it's approved — they can return it for correction.

docs.title: Command Dashboard
docs.text: The Command Dashboard is your primary hub in COMPASS. It's the first page you see after logging in as CO or XO, and gives you a full operational picture of your ship at a glance.

docs.title: Pending Actions
docs.text: Shows promotion and award submissions that require your attention, with a direct action button for each. If you have pending items, this panel will always be visible on the dashboard. Clearing your pending actions regularly keeps the workflow moving for your crew.

docs.title: SFDPP Compliance
docs.text:
Shows whether all role holders (CO, XO, and department heads) have completed current SFDPP privacy training. Displays a compliance percentage and a View all link to see the full breakdown.

Tip

SFDPP compliance is required for command roles. If this shows less than 100%, follow up with the listed crew members before your next report cycle.

docs.title: Crew by Department
docs.text: A horizontal bar chart showing how many crew are assigned to each department. Also shows the count of crew not yet assigned to any department — a useful indicator that your roster needs attention.

docs.title: Recent Activity
docs.text: The bottom of the dashboard shows a timestamped feed of recent platform activity — profile updates, new crew additions, event entries, and more. Useful for keeping tabs on what's been entered (or not entered) without digging into individual records.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
The left sidebar provides access to all COMPASS sections. The top of the sidebar shows your ship name and your current role. As CO or XO, you'll see all sections. Crew members see a reduced set.

Note

If you hold both a ship-level role (CO/XO) and a regional role (RC/VRC), you'll see both the Command Dashboard and Regional Dashboard in the navigation.

docs.title: Crew Transfers
docs.text:
Members move between chapters in COMPASS by following db.sfi.org, the official STARFLEET member database. There is nothing for a CO to approve. This page explains what you see when crew arrive or leave, and who to ask when a move needs a hand.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: How transfers work now
docs.text:
A member's chapter is set on db.sfi.org, and under SFI policy they can change it at any time, for any reason. COMPASS follows db.sfi.org rather than making its own decision:

  1. The member chooses a new ship in COMPASS (or leaves without one).
  2. COMPASS shows them exactly what to change on db.sfi.org.
  3. Once db.sfi.org shows the change, COMPASS completes the move — straight away if the member clicks check now, otherwise overnight.

Until db.sfi.org changes, the member stays where they are. The member's side of this is described in Joining or Changing Ships.

Older guidance

Earlier versions of COMPASS had receiving COs confirm transfers, and RCs approve moves between regions. That approval step no longer exists.

docs.title: Crew on their way to you
docs.text:
When someone picks your ship, your command team is told they're on their way, and Incoming Crew appears in your left navigation with a count.

The page lists each member heading your way: their name and SCC, their rank, the ship they're coming from, when they started, and Waiting for db.sfi.org. It also shows the exact chapter name they've been asked to choose on db.sfi.org, which is useful if they ask you for help.

Below that, Recent shows the members who have arrived (or cancelled) and how each move was completed — for example, Confirmed by your ship roster import.

You don't need to do anything. When db.sfi.org shows the change, COMPASS adds them to your roster and lets you know. If someone seems stuck, the usual cause is that they haven't changed their chapter on db.sfi.org yet; point them to the steps on their request page.

The Incoming Crew link only appears while someone is on their way. You (the CO and XO) see it.

docs.title: Crew leaving your ship
docs.text:
A member leaves from Leave Ship on their record or Profile, choosing another COMPASS ship, becoming unassigned, or a chapter that isn't on COMPASS. Their assignment on your ship closes once db.sfi.org shows the change. Any positions, department assignments and ship roles they held on your ship end at the same time.

Both the CO and the XO are told about every arrival and departure. If your ship has no CO — including when the CO is the one leaving — your Regional Coordinator is told as well.

Their history — service, awards, points, rank — goes with them.

docs.title: Seeing a member's moves
docs.text: Open a member's crew record and click Transfer History to see every move they've requested or made.

docs.title: Direct transfers
docs.text:
A Direct Transfer moves a member to a ship immediately, without waiting for db.sfi.org. It's an administrative tool for regional staff (the RC, VRC, RCOS and RCOO), used for things like a decommissioned chapter or regional rebalancing. COs and XOs don't have it.

If a member's move needs to happen right away, ask your Regional Coordinator.

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
A new member appeared on our roster without going through Incoming Crew. That's normal. Members also arrive through your roster import, which picks up anyone db.sfi.org lists on your chapter, and when a member sets up their account with db.sfi.org and db.sfi.org shows them on your ship. You're told either way.

I was asked to confirm whether our ship was renamed. A crew member told COMPASS that db.sfi.org shows your ship under a different name. Run a roster import: if db.sfi.org has renamed the ship, the import offers to rename it in COMPASS. See If your ship has been renamed.

Someone says they've changed their chapter but they're still on their old ship in COMPASS. Ask them to open their request and click I've changed it — check now. If db.sfi.org shows the change, the move completes immediately. Otherwise COMPASS checks overnight.

Can I stop someone transferring to my ship? No. A member's chapter is their choice under SFI policy.

docs.title: Delegating Command Authority
docs.text:
Some things in COMPASS only the Commanding Officer can do. That is usually right — but not always. A CO goes on vacation, has a medical stretch, deploys, or simply finds the platform more work than it is worth. Meanwhile promotions sit unapproved and award nominations go stale.

Command Action Delegation lets a CO hand specific authority to their XO — or, for events, to OPS and SO as well. The CO decides what to grant, and can take it back at any moment.

Delegation does not transfer command

Nothing here changes who commands the chapter. It grants the ability to perform specific actions in COMPASS, nothing more. The CO remains the CO, keeps every one of these abilities themselves, and is the only person who can change these settings.

docs.title: Where to Find It
docs.text:
Go to Command Dashboard → Ship Settings and scroll to Command Action Delegation.

Only the CO sees this card. An officer holding delegated authority cannot open it, and so cannot widen their own grant or hand authority to someone else.

docs.title: Events — XO, OPS, or SO
docs.text:
Action What it allows Approve / Reject Events Act on events crew members have submitted Delete Events Remove events from the ship calendar Add Shared Events Browse events shared by other chapters and add them to your calendar

Edit Events shows a locked checkmark. Your XO, OPS, and SO can already edit events platform-wide — that is not something the CO grants, and it cannot be revoked here.

docs.title: Promotions — XO only
docs.text:
Action What it allows Approve / Reject Promotions Act on promotions submitted for your crew, and give chapter input on region-initiated promotions

Promotions are XO-only, matching how SFI itself handles this: XOs already hold promotion authority on the member portal. OPS and SO are not offered.

docs.title: Awards — XO only
docs.text:
Action What it allows Approve / Reject Nominations Act on award nominations submitted for your crew Present Awards Record awards as presented Submit Awards to SFI Send approved nominations on to STARFLEET

These three are the only award functions restricted to the CO. Everything else — nominating, giving awards, managing your ship's award catalog, setting point overrides — your XO can already do without any grant.

docs.title: Granting and Revoking
docs.text:
Check the boxes you want, then click Save Delegation Settings. Changes take effect immediately — the officer does not need to log out and back in.

Revoking works the same way: uncheck the box and save. The officer loses that ability at once.

Turn it on before you leave, not after

Delegation is easiest to set up while you still have time to check it worked. If you know you'll be away, grant what your XO will need before you go rather than trying to sort it out from a phone in an airport.

docs.title: What Your XO Sees
docs.text:
Before you grant anything, your XO can already see the pending queues — the Pending Approvals tab under Promotions, and pending nominations under Awards. They have always been able to see these. What they lack is any way to act: no Approve button, no Reject button.

After you grant, those buttons appear. Your XO works the same screens you do, in exactly the same way.

Officers holding delegated authority also start receiving the pending-action notifications you get — the push and email alerts telling them something is waiting. Without that, they could act but would never know there was anything to act on.

docs.title: Limits That Always Apply
docs.text:
A few things hold regardless of what is granted:

  • No acting on yourself. An officer working under delegated authority cannot approve their own promotion or their own award nomination.
  • Your chapter only. Delegated authority stops at your ship. It never extends to another chapter's crew, even for a member the officer knows.
  • Per ship. A grant applies to the ship it was made on. An officer serving on two ships holds only what each CO granted separately.
  • The CO keeps everything. Granting an ability never removes it from the CO.

Every action taken under delegation is recorded as such. The record shows both who performed it and that it was done under delegated authority rather than by the officer's own permission — useful later when reconstructing who did what and why.

docs.title: Speaking to the Region
docs.text:
Promotion delegation includes one thing worth understanding before you grant it.

When a Regional Coordinator initiates a promotion for one of your members, COMPASS asks the chapter for input — a recommendation, or chapter-accomplishment examples. With promotion authority delegated, your XO answers those requests on behalf of the chapter, and the RC sees the chapter's response.

This is deliberate. The moment a CO is unavailable is exactly when a region-initiated promotion would otherwise stall. But it does mean your XO speaks for the chapter to the region, so grant it to someone you would trust to do that.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
My XO says the Approve button still isn't there. Confirm the box is checked and saved on your ship's settings — the card always edits the ship you command. Then have them reload the page. If they serve on more than one ship, the grant only applies to the one you made it on.

I unchecked a box but it came back. Make sure you clicked Save Delegation Settings after unchecking. The grid does not save on click.

My XO can't approve a particular promotion. Check whether the promotion is theirs. An officer cannot act on their own promotion under delegated authority — that one has to come to you.

I don't see the Command Action Delegation card at all. Only the CO sees it. If you are the XO, this is expected. If you are the CO and it is missing, your COMPASS role may not be set to CO — check Crew Roster or contact your RC.

docs.title: Departments
docs.text:
Departments let you organise your crew the way your chapter actually runs: Command, Engineering, Medical, a gaming group, an away team, whatever fits. Each department has members, an optional department head, and its own activity report.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Member names are blurred.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Task Who Create, edit or delete departments CO, XO Set the department head CO, XO Assign or remove members CO, XO, SO, and department heads Approve requests to join CO, XO, SO, and the department's head See a department's activity report CO, XO, and that department's head Request to join a department Any crew member

docs.title: Your departments
docs.text:
Go to Departments in the left navigation.

Each card shows the department's colour, how many crew are in it, its description, and its head. Click a card to open the department.

If you also hold a regional or fleet role, sections for regional departments and fleet auxiliaries appear below your ship's.

docs.title: Creating a department
docs.text:
1. On the Departments page, click + New Ship Department.
  2. Enter a name and an optional description, and pick a colour.
  3. Save.

To change these later, open the department and click Edit Department. Delete removes the department; its members aren't affected in any other way.

docs.title: Managing a department
docs.text: Open a department to see its page.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
1. Click + Assign Member.
  2. Choose a crew member.
  3. Optionally give them a Role/Position within the department, such as "Chief Engineer" or "Assistant".
  4. Tick Set as primary department if this is their main department. A member can belong to several departments, but only one is primary.
  5. Click Assign.

Click Remove next to a member to take them out of the department.

docs.title: Department head
docs.text: Under Department Head, click Assign Head and choose a member. The head can approve join requests and see the department's activity report.

docs.title: Fleet connection
docs.text:
Many STARFLEET fleet-level auxiliaries — such as the STARFLEET Tactical Auxiliary — have a matching fleet department in COMPASS. Click Connect to Fleet to link your ship's department to it.

Connecting lets the fleet department see your department as part of its network. It doesn't move or share any members. Disconnect removes the link at any time.

docs.title: Department dashboard
docs.text:
Click View Dashboard on a department page for an at-a-glance view:

  • Total members, with primary and secondary assignments
  • The department head
  • Recent Assignments and Recent Departures in the last 30 days
  • If connected to a fleet department: network members, linked ships, and supporting ships across the whole network

docs.title: Activity report
docs.text:
Click Activity Report on a department page to see what the department's members have been doing.

  1. Choose a Time Period: the last 1, 2, 3 or 6 months. The default is 2 months.
  2. Read the summary: events with department participation, total attendances, and the most active member.
  3. Scroll down for each member's events attended, points earned and participation rate, and for a list of every event with which department members attended.

Copy Report Data and Copy Roster Data copy the report and the department roster as plain text, ready to paste into a fleet auxiliary report or an email. The roster includes each member's rank, SCC and membership expiration.

Tip

Fleet auxiliaries often ask for a periodic report. Run the activity report for the period they ask about and paste the copied text into their form.

docs.title: Requests to join
docs.text:
Crew members who open a department they don't belong to see a Request to Join button, with an optional message.

Pending requests appear in the Notifications panel on the Crew Dashboard of everyone who can approve them — the CO, XO and SO for any department, and each department head for their own. The notice links to the department, where you Approve or Deny the request.

No email or push notice is sent for join requests, so check your dashboard. The member sees Request Pending on the department page until you decide.

docs.title: Departments elsewhere in COMPASS
docs.text:
• The Command Dashboard shows a Crew by Department chart, including how many crew aren't in any department yet.
  • Each member's departments appear on their crew record and their dashboard.

docs.title: Opening Event Points
docs.text:
Most chapters do not join COMPASS on their founding day. They arrive with years of history — meetings held, events run, crew who have earned hundreds of activity points that exist only in a spreadsheet or the outgoing CO's memory.

Entering all of that event by event is not realistic. Event point adjustments let you give your crew a starting balance in one pass, so promotions calculate correctly from day one without reconstructing the past.

This is not a separate pool

An adjustment is folded into the member's event point total. A member with 12 recorded points and a 45-point adjustment simply has 57 event points. Nothing anywhere shows the two figures apart.

docs.title: When You Would Use This
docs.text:
• Joining COMPASS — give the roster the balance they carried in. This is the main case.
  • Correcting a recording error — an event was entered twice, or attendance was recorded for the wrong person.
  • Reconciling with chapter records — your own records and COMPASS disagree, and yours are right.

If you simply forgot to record a recent event, enter the event instead. Adjustments are for history you cannot reasonably reconstruct.

docs.title: The Prompt on Your Roster
docs.text:
New chapters see a prompt at the top of the Crew Roster.

Get Started opens the bulk entry page. Dismiss hides the prompt for you.

The prompt disappears on its own once your chapter records its first adjustment, so it is not something you have to clear. Dismissing costs you nothing either — the tool stays available under Ship Settings permanently.

Dismissal is per person

If you dismiss it, your XO still sees it, and the other way round. Neither of you can hide it from the other.

docs.title: Entering Balances for the Whole Roster
docs.text:
The bulk page lists your active roster with one entry box per member.

Reason and Effective Date apply to every member you enter on this page. One reason covers the batch — something like Points carried over from chapter records — so you are not typing it thirty times.

Current shows each member's event points as they stand now, so you can see what you are adding to.

In the Adjustment box, enter a positive number to add points or a negative number to remove them. Leave blank anyone you are not adjusting — blanks are skipped, so a roster of forty where six need changes means filling in six boxes.

The counter above the button tracks how many entries you have made. Click Record Adjustments and confirm.

Entries cannot be edited or deleted

Once recorded, an adjustment is permanent. To reverse one, record a new adjustment with the opposite sign — enter -45 to undo a +45. This is deliberate: it keeps an honest history of what was changed and when, rather than letting the record be quietly rewritten.

docs.title: Adjusting One Member
docs.text:
For a single member, open their crew profile and scroll to Event Point Adjustments below their event participation. Same fields — points, date, reason — plus a history of every adjustment on that member showing who made it.

The history panel is visible only to the CO and XO.

docs.title: Finding It Later
docs.text: The prompt on your roster goes away, but the tool does not. It lives at Command Dashboard → Ship Settings → Event Point Adjustments alongside your other point configuration.

docs.title: Who Can Do This
docs.text:
The CO and XO. Not OPS, SO, or department heads.

The reasoning: recording points for an event that actually happened is an operations task, and plenty of people can do it. Asserting points that were never recorded in COMPASS is a command decision, and it belongs with command.

docs.title: What This Does Not Change
docs.text:
Adjustments affect event points only. They do not touch academy points, award points, permanent points, or time in grade. A member short on time in grade stays short on time in grade no matter what you enter here.

They also do not appear as attendance. Your event statistics, attendance counts, and uniform compliance figures are unaffected — those reflect events that actually happened.

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
How do I work out what to give someone? Whatever your chapter's own records say they had earned. There is no formula COMPASS can supply — it never saw those events. If your records are approximate, be conservative: a member who is slightly under can earn the difference, while one who is over may get promoted early.

Can I give someone a negative balance? Yes, and the total can go below zero if you over-correct. That is a real state, not an error, and it means the member earns their way back up before qualifying. If it was not what you intended, record another adjustment to bring them back.

What happens to these points at promotion? Nothing special. Adjusted points are event points, and they are spent on promotion exactly as recorded ones are.

Someone transferred in from another chapter — do their points follow? Yes. Event points, including adjustments, follow the member rather than staying with the chapter.

Is there a record of who did this? Yes. Every adjustment stores the points, reason, date, and the officer who entered it, and the entry cannot be edited or removed. The per-member history on the crew profile shows all of it.

docs.title: Sharing Events Between Chapters
docs.text:
Some events are worth more than one chapter. A charity drive, a convention appearance, a virtual game night, a commissioning ceremony — any of these might draw members from neighboring chapters if they knew about it.

Event sharing lets your ship publish one of its events to your region or to the entire fleet. Officers at other chapters can then add it to their own calendar, where their crew RSVP and earn attendance credit exactly as they would for any other event.

Sharing publishes a listing — it does not touch anyone's calendar

Sharing an event does not add it to another chapter's calendar. It makes the event visible to officers at other chapters, who decide for themselves whether to add it. Nothing appears on another ship's roster unless their command chooses it.

docs.title: Who Can Do What
docs.text:
Action Who Share an event with your region CO, XO Share an event with the entire fleet CO View and add events shared by other chapters CO, XO — plus any officer the CO delegates it to

Crew members never see the shared events list. They see only the events their own command has added to the ship calendar.

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the event
docs.text:
Open an approved event on your ship from Events. In the right-hand column, between Quick Stats and Actions, you'll find the Sharing panel showing the current state.

Click Share Event.

docs.title: Step 2 — Choose your audience
docs.text:
The sharing page offers the options your permissions allow.

  • Share With My Region — visible to chapters in your region only. The right choice for most in-person events, since geography does the filtering for you.
  • Share With Entire Fleet — visible to every chapter. Best reserved for virtual events, major conventions, and anything genuinely open to members anywhere.

docs.title: Step 3 — Manage the share
docs.text:
Once published, the page shows the current scope and tracks uptake.

From here you can:

  • Widen to Entire Fleet — promote a regional share fleet-wide
  • Narrow to My Region — pull a fleet share back to your region
  • Stop Sharing — withdraw the listing entirely

Tip

Widening and narrowing keep the same listing, so chapters that already added your event stay connected to it. You don't lose anyone by changing your mind about the audience.

docs.title: Tracking Who's Coming
docs.text:
As other chapters add your event, the sharing page builds a headcount broken down by chapter.

This is what makes sharing useful to a host. If you're reserving tables or buying supplies, knowing that three chapters are bringing eleven people between them is the number you actually need.

When more than two regions are represented, the breakdown groups by region with a subtotal for each.

Counts only — never names

You see how many members each chapter is bringing. You never see who they are. Individual member names are never shared between chapters.

The page also lists every chapter that has added your event — including chapters that added it but whose crew haven't RSVP'd yet.

docs.title: Adding an Event Another Chapter Has Shared
docs.text:
From Events, click Shared Regional/Fleet Events, then choose the Shared by Chapters tab.

Each listing shows the hosting chapter, the date, and how many chapters have already added it. Open one and click Add to [Your Ship].

docs.title: What happens when you add it
docs.text:
Adding creates a real event on your own calendar, owned by your ship:

  • Your crew RSVP and are marked attended on your copy
  • Attendance and points flow into your roster and reports exactly like any other event
  • The host chapter sees your headcount as a number and nothing more

Added events appear on your Events list and calendar with a marker showing where they came from.

docs.title: Badges
docs.text: Badge Meaning ⇧ Shared · Region or ⇧ Shared · Fleet Your ship shared this event outward ⇩ USS [Chapter] Your ship added this event from another chapter

docs.title: Staying in sync
docs.text: If the host chapter changes the date, location, or details, your copy updates automatically. If you'd rather freeze your copy — say your chapter is doing a variation on the host's plan — open the event and turn off auto sync. Your copy then stops following the host's changes.

docs.title: Delegating Access
docs.text:
If you'd rather your XO, OPS, or SO officer handle browsing and adding shared events, go to Ship Settings → Command Action Delegation and check Add Shared Events for that role.

The same grid controls approving and deleting events. Granting shared-event access does not grant either of those. See Delegating Command Authority for the full picture, including what can be delegated for promotions and awards.

docs.title: What Appears in the List
docs.text:
The shared list shows only events still worth adding: upcoming events, plus anything from the last 24 hours.

The one-day grace window exists so a chapter can still add an event that happened yesterday and record attendance for it. Beyond that, events drop off to keep the list readable. Multi-day events stay listed until their end date passes.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
I don't see a Sharing panel on my event. Sharing requires the event to be approved first — pending and rejected events cannot be shared. You also need CO or XO on the ship that owns the event; you can only share your own chapter's events.

I shared an event and it disappeared from the list. Three things withdraw a listing automatically: deleting the source event, setting it back to pending, or having it rejected. Re-approve the event and share it again if this wasn't intentional.

Another chapter added my event, then I cancelled it. What happens to them? Cancelling or deleting your event withdraws the listing so nobody else can add it, but chapters that already added it keep their copy and any attendance already recorded. Contact them directly — withdrawing a listing does not notify anyone.

A chapter outside my region can't see my event. Working as intended. Region-scoped shares are visible only within your region. Use Widen to Entire Fleet for broader reach.

Our OPS officer can't see the Shared by Chapters tab. Only CO and XO have that access by default. Grant it in Ship Settings → Event Delegation.

I added a shared event by mistake. Delete it from your calendar like any other event. This affects only your copy — the host chapter and every other chapter are untouched.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Event tracking builds the activity record that drives promotion eligibility, award nominations, and monthly reports. Every meeting, activity, and convention appearance should be logged.

Go to Events in the left navigation.

docs.title: Creating an Event
docs.text:
Click Create Event from the Events page.

Required fields:

  • Event Name — A descriptive title (e.g., "June Monthly Meeting", "Regional Summit 2026")
  • Event Type — Determines point value (see below)
  • Event Date — The date the event takes (or took) place

Optional fields:

  • Event Time — Leave it blank for an all-day event. An all-day event shows only its date, with no time, everywhere in COMPASS and in calendar feeds. Enter a time and it is shown to each member in their own time zone.
  • End Date / End Time — For multi-day events such as conventions.
  • Location and Description
  • Counts for Attendance Tracking — Pre-set from the event type. Leave it on for events where you take attendance; turn it off for things like articles or recruiting credit.
  • Event Visibility
  • Charity Amount Raised — For charity events.
  • Attendance — For an event that has already happened, you can check off who attended right on the create form. You can also record it later.

New events are created as pending and are approved by an officer who holds event-approval authority for the ship. Officers who can approve will see an Approve Event button on the event page.

docs.title: Repeating Events
docs.text:
If your chapter meets on a regular schedule, create the meeting once as a repeating event instead of entering every date by hand.

On the create form, use the Repeats section:

Option What it does Does not repeat A single event (the default). Daily Every day. Weekly Every week, on one or more days you pick under On (e.g. Tue and Thu). Every other week Every second week, on the days you pick. Monthly Once a month. The choices are built from the event date you entered — see below.

Monthly choices. Pick an Event Date first; COMPASS then offers the patterns that fit it. For a date of Saturday, October 31, for example, you would be offered:

  • The 5th Saturday (only months that have one)
  • The last Saturday
  • The 31st — months without a 31st are skipped, not moved
  • The last day of the month

A date in the first four weeks offers "The 1st/2nd/3rd/4th weekday" instead. If you want "the end of the month" every month, choose The last day of the month, not the 31st.

Ends. Choose when the series stops:

  • Never — keeps going until you end it
  • On a specific date
  • After a number of occurrences (up to 500)

Preview. As you fill in the options, a Preview lists the actual dates that will be created, and lists any months that will be skipped. Check it before you submit — it is calculated by the same code that creates the events, so what you see is what you get.

Click Create Repeating Event to save.

docs.title: Rules for repeating events
docs.text:
• A repeating event must start today or later, and needs a start time. To record meetings that already happened, enter them as single events.
  • Attendance and charity amounts are not entered on the create form. Each date is its own event; record attendance on each one after it happens.
  • COMPASS creates the dates about six months ahead and tops them up automatically each night, so a "Never" series always has the next half year on the calendar.
  • Approval happens once, for the whole series. On any occurrence of a pending series, an approver will see Approve Series. Approving it approves every upcoming occurrence. Past occurrences are not changed.

On each occurrence's page, a Repeating event banner describes the pattern (e.g. "Every week on Tuesday") and shows whether the series is pending or has ended.

docs.title: Editing a Repeating Event
docs.text:
Open the occurrence you want to change and click Edit Event. The edit page asks what the change applies to:

  • This event only — changes just this date. Use this to move one meeting or change its location.
  • This and following occurrences — changes this date and every one after it.
  • All future occurrences — changes every occurrence that hasn't started yet, including ones earlier than the one you opened.

When you choose one of the series options, the Repeats section appears so you can change the pattern itself (for example, moving from Tuesdays to Thursdays, or setting an end date).

Things to know:

  • Occurrences that have already started are never changed by a series edit. Your history stays exactly as it happened.
  • A series edit overrides one-off changes to future dates. If you moved next week's meeting by hand and then edit "all future occurrences", next week follows the new series settings.
  • Before you save, COMPASS shows what the change will do — how many dates are affected, and whether any of them already have attendance recorded.

docs.title: Seeing Who's Coming
docs.text:
The RSVP section on an event shows totals to everyone. To see who responded, click View details on the event (or View Details on the attendance page).

The RSVP page shows counts for Attending, Maybe, Not Attending and No Response — active crew who haven't answered — then lists each person under their answer, with when they responded.

Names are visible to your command team, regional officers over your chapter, and whoever created the event. Use the list to plan, and as a checklist when you record attendance afterwards. An RSVP isn't attendance: points only come from the attendance you record.

docs.title: RSVPs and Change Notices
docs.text:
Events that count for attendance show an RSVP section, so crew can say whether they are attending. RSVP closes 24 hours after the event starts.

When a chapter event — single or repeating — moves (date, time, or switching to/from all-day), changes location, or is cancelled, every member who RSVP'd Attending or Maybe is notified automatically.

  • Renaming an event or editing its description does not notify anyone.
  • Nobody is notified about a change they made themselves, and events already past are skipped.
  • A series edit that touches several dates a member RSVP'd to arrives as one message listing each changed date, not one message per date.
  • Members control this in their notification preferences under Event Changes.

docs.title: Event Types
docs.text:
Each event type has a base point value, a uniform multiplier, and a default for whether it counts for attendance. Common types include Meeting or Event, Games with Crewmates, Attend a convention, Participating in charity event, Participating in community service, and Plan or Host an event.

The full list, with your ship's values, is in Ship Settings → Event Points — see Ship Settings.

docs.title: Recording Attendance
docs.text:
Open the event and click Record Attendance (or Edit Attendance once some has been entered). Check each crew member who attended, and mark who was in uniform.

Tip

Enter attendance the same day or the next morning. Remembering who attended two weeks later is much harder — and missing attendance means missing points toward promotion eligibility.

docs.title: Plan / Host Credit
docs.text:
Members who plan or host an event can be credited directly on that event — you no longer need to create a separate "Plan or Host an event" entry just to give someone that credit.

On any event you can manage (you hold attendance permission, or you created the event), open the event and click Plan / Host Credit. A window lists your active crew — check everyone who planned or hosted, then click Save Host Credit.

  • No one, one, or many members can be credited on a single event.
  • Host credit is worth the "Plan or Host an event" point value, awarded on top of any attendance points. A member who both attended and hosted receives both.
  • Unchecking everyone and saving removes all host credit from the event.

Credited members appear in a Planned / Hosted By list on the event page, and their host points flow into promotion totals and reports automatically. Host credit is not attendance — it will not inflate attendance counts or uniform-compliance figures.

Note

The standalone "Plan or Host an event" event type still works if you prefer it. This feature simply lets you record the same credit on the real event instead of entering a duplicate.

docs.title: Editing or Deleting an Event
docs.text:
Open the event from the Events list and click Edit Event to change any details. Events can be deleted if entered in error, but deletion is permanent — there's no undo.

Deleting a repeating event opens a window with the same choices as editing: This event only, This and following occurrences, or All future occurrences. It tells you how many dates will be removed. If any of them already have attendance recorded, you must tick a box confirming you want those records deleted too. Deleting "this event only" removes that one date for good — it will not be recreated.

Warning

Deleting an event removes all attendance records and the associated points for all attendees. If the event was just entered with the wrong date or wrong type, edit it rather than deleting and re-entering.

docs.title: Sharing Events With Other Chapters
docs.text: Your ship can publish an event to your region or the whole fleet so other chapters can add it to their own calendars — and you can add events other chapters have shared. See Sharing Events Between Chapters.

docs.title: How Events Drive Promotions
docs.text: Each attended event awards the attending crew member a number of activity points, based on the event type's configured point value. These points accumulate toward promotion eligibility requirements. You can see a member's point total and the events driving it on their crew record.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
I forgot to log an event from last month. Enter it as a single event with the correct past date — no problem. Only repeating events are limited to starting today or later.

A member's attendance isn't showing in their promotion record. Open the event and verify they're checked in the attendance list. Also check that the event is approved and that the event type has a non-zero point value in Ship Settings.

I entered the wrong event type and points were awarded incorrectly. Edit the event and change the type. Points will recalculate automatically.

My monthly meeting skipped a month. You probably picked a specific date such as The 31st, or The 5th Saturday, which some months don't have. The Preview lists skipped months. Edit All future occurrences and choose The last day of the month or a weekday pattern instead.

I changed one meeting, then edited the series, and my change disappeared. That's by design — series edits apply to every future date. Make the one-off change again with This event only.

An event I entered with no time used to show "12:00 AM". Events entered without a time are now true all-day events and show the date only.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide walks you through setting up your ship in COMPASS for the first time. The process takes about five minutes and is largely automatic — COMPASS pulls your ship data and crew roster directly from the SFI Members Portal.

docs.title: Before You Begin
docs.text:
You'll need:

  • Your db.sfi.org username and password (your SFI database credentials — not a COMPASS password)
  • To be listed as CO or XO of your chapter in db.sfi.org — setup will fail if you're not

These are your SFI credentials, not a COMPASS account

COMPASS uses your db.sfi.org credentials once to pull your chapter info and roster. They are never stored. If you don't have db.sfi.org credentials, log in at db.sfi.org first to set them up.

docs.title: Step 1 — Enter Your SFI Credentials
docs.text:
Go to compass.sfi.org and click Add Your Ship to COMPASS on the login page.

Enter your db.sfi.org username and password and click Connect to SFI. COMPASS authenticates against the SFI database and fetches your chapter information and roster. A loading spinner will appear while it works.

Only CO or XO can run setup

COMPASS verifies your role against db.sfi.org. If you're not listed as CO or XO, you'll see an error: "Only the Commanding Officer or Executive Officer can set up a ship in COMPASS." Have your CO or XO run setup instead.

Common errors at this step:

  • "Unable to authenticate" — double-check your db.sfi.org username and password. Log in at db.sfi.org directly to confirm they work.
  • "Unable to retrieve chapter information" — your account authenticated but has no CO/XO role on file. Contact your RC.

docs.title: Step 2 — Select Your Chapter (if prompted)
docs.text: If your SFI account is associated with more than one chapter, COMPASS will show a chapter selection screen. Pick the chapter you're setting up and continue. If you only have one chapter, this step is skipped automatically.

docs.title: Step 3 — Review Your Ship Information
docs.text:
COMPASS displays a Review & Confirm page showing everything pulled from db.sfi.org.

The page shows:

  • Ship Information — name, registry, class, region, type, commissioned date, charter city
  • Command Staff — CO and XO with SCCs; your name will have a You badge
  • Crew Roster Preview — every member COMPASS found in your db.sfi.org roster, with position, rank, name, and SCC

Review this carefully. If the ship name, registry, or command staff looks wrong, click ← Start Over and contact your RC — the data comes directly from db.sfi.org, so any errors need to be corrected there first.

Ship already exists in COMPASS

If your ship has already been set up, you'll see an orange warning banner and the Create Ship button won't appear. Contact your RC to get access to the existing record.

docs.title: Step 4 — Create Ship & Import Crew
docs.text:
If everything looks correct, click Create Ship & Import Crew.

COMPASS will:

  1. Create your ship record — name, registry, class, region, and all chapter details
  2. Import your entire crew roster — all members from db.sfi.org are added with their ranks, positions, and SCCs
  3. Create your COMPASS account — you're automatically logged in after setup
  4. Sync your eligibility data — OTS/OCC completions and academy records are pulled from db.sfi.org

Don't close the page

A loading spinner appears while provisioning runs. This can take 10–15 seconds depending on roster size. Don't close or refresh the page while it's working.

docs.title: Step 5 — You're In
docs.text: On success, COMPASS redirects you to the Command Dashboard with a confirmation message. Your ship is live with your full roster already imported.

docs.title: After Setup — What to Do Next
Set Your Password
docs.text: Your COMPASS account was created automatically. Go to Profile → Change Password and set a permanent password before logging out.

docs.title: Verify Your Roster
docs.text: Go to Crew and scan through your imported roster. Check that all active members are present and ranks look correct. If someone is missing, it means they weren't on your chapter's roster in db.sfi.org.

docs.title: Invite Your XO
docs.text: Your XO was imported as a crew member but may not have a COMPASS account yet. Direct them to compass.sfi.org to register — they'll need to use the same email or SCC on file. Their command permissions apply automatically once their account is active.

docs.title: Log Your First Event
docs.text: Go to Events → Create Event and enter your most recent ship meeting. See the Events Guide.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Setup failed partway through. The setup runs as a single transaction — if anything fails, nothing is saved. You can safely run it again from the start.

My roster shows 0 members. Your chapter may not have a roster on file in db.sfi.org. Your ship record will still be created — add crew manually via Crew → Add Member.

I already have a COMPASS account. That's fine — COMPASS detects your existing account by SCC and links it to the new ship rather than creating a duplicate.

My ship was previously in COMPASS but was withdrawn. COMPASS reactivates it automatically if your registry matches a withdrawn ship. Historical data (awards, promotion history, events) is fully preserved. Crew members will need to rejoin through the normal join request process.

docs.title: Promotions
docs.text:
COMPASS manages the full promotion workflow from eligibility checking through approval and SFI database update. This page covers the complete process for both standard promotions (O-1 through O-5) and flag officer promotions (O-6 and above).

Go to Promotions in the left navigation to open the Promotion Eligibility Report.

Can't approve promotions yourself?

Approving promotions is a CO ability, but a CO can delegate it to their XO — see Delegating Command Authority.

docs.title: The Promotion Eligibility Report
docs.text:
The report has three tabs:

Tab What It Shows Eligibility All crew with current eligibility status, points, and time-in-grade Pending Promotions submitted and awaiting regional review History All past promotions for your ship

docs.title: Standard Promotions (E-1 through O-5)
docs.text: These promotions cover all Cadet (C-1 through C-6), Enlisted (E-1 through E-9), and junior Officer (O-1 through O-5) ranks. They are approved directly by the ship CO in COMPASS — no regional review required.

docs.title: Step 1 — Check Eligibility
docs.text: On the Eligibility tab, each crew member shows their current rank, time-in-grade, point totals, and eligibility status. A Promote button appears on rows where all requirements are met.

docs.title: Step 2 — Open the Promotion Form
docs.text:
Click Promote to open the promotion dialog for that crew member.

The form shows:

  • Available Points — Event + Academy points and Awards + Permanent points broken out separately
  • Promote To — Target rank, pre-selected as the next eligible rank
  • Points to Spend — How many Event + Academy points will be consumed by this promotion
  • Requirements — All requirements with green checkmarks confirming they're met
  • Promotion Date — Defaults to today; can be set to any past or future date
  • Effective Time — Optional; leave blank to apply at the start of the promotion date
  • TIG Waiver — Reduces time-in-grade requirement by 50% for extraordinary service
  • Notes — Optional internal notes visible to the RC

docs.title: Step 3 — Approve
docs.text: Click Approve Now. The promotion is applied immediately — no regional review required. The member's rank updates in COMPASS and they receive an email notification.

docs.title: O-6 Promotions (Captain)
docs.text: Promotion to Captain (O-6) requires RC approval. The form works the same as standard promotions but the submission routes to the RC rather than approving immediately.

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Promotion Form
docs.text: Click Promote on the eligible crew member. The O-6 form looks similar to a standard promotion.

docs.title: Step 2 — Submit for RC Approval
docs.text: Click Approve Now to submit. The promotion routes to the RC's regional queue rather than approving immediately. The member is notified and the promotion appears in your Pending tab.

docs.title: Flag Officer Promotions (O-7 and above)
docs.text: Promotions to Fleet Captain (O-7) and above follow an extended workflow with additional narrative questions and SFI Fleet Command involvement.

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Promotion Form
docs.text:
The form opens the same way but shows additional O-7+ content at the bottom.

Notice the differences from a standard promotion:

  • Points to Spend is 0 — permanent points drive eligibility, not event points
  • The TIG Waiver description changes to "Extraordinary Service – reduces TIG by 6 months"
  • An O-6+ Promotion – Commanding Officer Recommendation section appears at the bottom

docs.title: Step 2 — Complete the CO Recommendation
docs.text:
Scroll down to the CO Recommendation section. This is required for all O-7+ promotions.

First, select your recommendation:

  • ✓ Recommend Approval — You support this promotion
  • ✗ Don't Recommend Approval — You do not support it (rare, but available)

Then complete the Flag Promotion Nomination Form Questions. These answers are pre-filled onto the official SFI Flag Promotion Nomination Form PDF and forwarded to the RC:

Question What to Include Q1. Nominator/Nominee Relationship Your role relative to the nominee (e.g., Commanding Officer) Q2. Why should this person be promoted? Their overall service record and qualities Q3. Specific examples benefiting their Chapter Concrete contributions to their ship Q4. Specific examples benefiting their Region Regional service, events, leadership Q5. Specific examples benefiting STARFLEET Fleet-level contributions Q7. Outside hobbies or activities Community activities relevant to their character Q8. Other awards or documentation Any additional supporting evidence

Write Substantive Answers

Flag promotion narratives are reviewed by your RC and by SFI Fleet Command. Vague answers delay approval. Write specific, concrete examples with dates where possible. The RC can edit answers inline before forwarding, but strong original submissions move faster.

Click Submit for RC Approval when complete.

docs.title: RC Review — O-6 Promotions
docs.text: Once submitted, the promotion appears in the RC's Regional Promotions queue under O-6 Pending Approval.

docs.title: RC Reviews the Submission
docs.text:
The RC opens the review panel showing the full submission — member details and nomination form answers.

The RC has three options:

  • Approve Promotion — Approves directly; rank updates in COMPASS immediately
  • Reject Promotion — Rejects with a reason sent back to the CO
  • Cancel — Closes without action

docs.title: RC Review — O-7+ Promotions
docs.text: For O-7 (Fleet Captain) and above, the RC cannot approve directly — these require SFI Fleet Command approval. The RC's role is to review, endorse, and forward the nomination.

docs.title: RC Reviews and Recommends to Fleet
docs.text:
The RC reviews the submission the same way as O-6, but the action buttons at the bottom are different.

The RC has three options:

  • Recommend to Fleet — Forwards the nomination to SFI Fleet Command with optional endorsement notes
  • Nomination Form — Downloads the pre-filled Flag Promotion Nomination Form PDF
  • Reject — Rejects the nomination at the regional level

docs.title: RC Recommends to Fleet
docs.text:
Clicking Recommend to Fleet opens a confirmation dialog where the RC can add optional recommendation notes to Fleet Command.

After clicking Recommend to Fleet, COMPASS returns to the Regional Promotions page with a confirmation banner. The promotion moves from the O-7+ Pending Recommendation queue into the Recently Actioned table with a status of Awaiting Fleet Decision.

From this view the RC can see:

  • The green confirmation banner confirming the nomination was sent to Fleet Command
  • Any remaining O-7+ promotions still needing action in the O-7+ Pending Recommendation queue
  • The Recently Actioned table showing the promotion with Awaiting Fleet Decision status
  • Two action buttons: Record Fleet Decision (for when Fleet responds) and Nomination Form (to download the PDF at any time)

The external approval process now continues outside COMPASS. SFI Fleet Command will review the nomination and respond. When they do, the RC returns here to record the outcome.

docs.title: The Flag Promotion Nomination Form PDF
docs.text:
At any point during review, the RC can download the pre-filled SFI Flag Promotion Nomination Form by clicking Nomination Form.

COMPASS pre-fills the entire form from data already in the system:

  • Nominee name, SCC, join date, email, region, and chapter
  • Chapter CO name and email
  • Current rank and rank date
  • Requested rank
  • All relevant positions held since last rank date (pulled from ship assignments)
  • OTS, OCC, and current SFDPP certification dates

This eliminates manual form-filling. The RC downloads and submits this PDF to SFI Membership Services as part of the external O-7+ approval process.

docs.title: Recording the Fleet Decision
docs.text:
Once SFI Fleet Command responds, the RC records the outcome back in COMPASS using the Record Fleet Decision button on the promotion row.

Select Approved or Rejected, add any notes from Fleet Command, and click Submit Decision. If approved, the member's rank updates in COMPASS and they are notified.

docs.title: Approval Workflow Summary
docs.text: Rank Approving Authority COMPASS Action Cadet (C-1 through C-6) Ship CO CO approves directly in COMPASS Enlisted (E-1 through E-9) Ship CO CO approves directly in COMPASS O-1 through O-5 Ship CO CO approves directly in COMPASS O-6 (Captain) RC RC approves directly in COMPASS O-7 (Fleet Captain) SFI Fleet Command RC recommends to Fleet; RC records decision O-8 (Commodore) SFI Fleet Command RC recommends to Fleet; RC records decision O-9 (Rear Admiral) SFI Fleet Command RC recommends to Fleet; RC records decision O-10 (Vice Admiral) Executive Committee RC recommends to Fleet; EC vote required O-11+ (Admiral and above) Executive Committee RC recommends to Fleet; EC vote required

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Member shows ineligible but should qualify. Check that all event attendance, academy completions, and awards are entered — missing data is the most common cause. Also confirm their OTS/OCC status is current via SFI Database Sync.

I need to correct a submission already sent to the RC. Contact your RC — they can edit narrative answers inline or return the submission for correction before approving.

The Flag Promotion PDF is missing positions held. Positions are pulled from COMPASS ship assignment records. If a position isn't showing, check that it's recorded in Ship Positions with the correct date range.

Status shows "Awaiting Fleet Decision" but Fleet has responded. The RC needs to record the fleet decision in COMPASS using the Record Fleet Decision button on that promotion row.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
COMPASS includes a full suite of reports for monitoring your ship's health, tracking crew activity, and generating required SFI submissions.

Go to Command Dashboard → Reports to reach the Reports & Analytics page.

docs.title: Crew Activity Report
docs.text:
Shows event participation rates, attendance streaks, active crew tracking, and an Inactive Crew Alert highlighting members who haven't attended any events in the selected period.

Use this report monthly to identify members who may be slipping into inactivity before they actually leave.

docs.title: Event Statistics Report
docs.text: Breaks down your events by type, attendance trends, and most-attended events over a selectable time period.

docs.title: Promotion Points Report
docs.text: Shows a detailed points breakdown for all crew members — event points, academy points, permanent points, and total — to help determine promotion eligibility at a glance.

docs.title: Points Accumulation Report
docs.text: Tracks recognition and promotion point trends across your crew over time.

docs.title: Academy Completion Report
docs.text: Shows OTS, OCC, and academy course completions by crew member. Useful for identifying who needs training to qualify for command roles.

docs.title: Membership Expiration Report
docs.text: Tracks crew members with memberships expiring in the next 60, 45, 30, 21, 14, or 7 days, and those already expired. Run this monthly before submitting reports to avoid losing crew to lapsed memberships.

docs.title: Community Service Hours Report
docs.text: Tracks volunteer hours from community service event types across your crew.

docs.title: Uniform Compliance Report
docs.text: Tracks uniform wearing rates and bonus points earned for crew who wear their uniform to events.

docs.title: Crew Platform Engagement
docs.text: Shows which crew members are actively logging into COMPASS and identifies dormant accounts — useful for following up with members who may not know the platform exists.

docs.title: Monthly Status Report (MSR)
docs.text:
Generates the MSR for SFI submission, listing current and previous month activity with participant counts.

Tip

Run the MSR report at the end of each month, review for accuracy, and submit to your RC. The RC manual requires monthly submission — COMPASS does the counting for you, but you still need to formally submit.

docs.title: Individual Crew Report
docs.text: A complete profile report for a specific crew member. Access this from the crew roster by clicking a member's name rather than from the main Reports page.

docs.title: Exporting Data
docs.text:
The bottom of the Reports page has three export buttons:

Export Contents Export Crew Roster Full crew list with ranks, statuses, and SCCs Export Events All events with dates, types, and attendance counts Export Participation Data Per-member event attendance and points data

Exports are CSV format, suitable for Excel or Google Sheets.

docs.title: Exporting One Member's Activity
docs.text:
To export a single crew member's activity for a date range — for a promotion packet, an award nomination, or a member who asks for their history:

  1. Open the member's crew record (click their name on the roster).

  2. Click Export Activity at the top right.

  3. Choose a Start Date and End Date. The window opens set to the last 30 days.

  4. Click Export CSV.

The file starts with the member's name, SCC and the period, then one row per item with its date, type, description, details, points and uniform:

  • Event participation, with the event type and whether they wore uniform
  • Awards received, with their point value
  • Promotions, shown as negative points (the points the promotion used)
  • Permanent points awarded, with their category

Academy courses aren't included, because COMPASS records academy totals rather than a date for each course.

Export Activity is available to the CO, XO, OPS and SO.

Adjusting points

To give a member (or your whole roster) a starting balance of event points, or to correct a recording error, use event point adjustments. See Opening Event Points.

docs.title: Managing Your Roster
docs.text:
Your crew roster is the foundation of everything in COMPASS — promotion eligibility, event attendance, awards, and reports all depend on an accurate roster.

Go to Crew Roster in the left navigation to view your full ship roster.

docs.title: Member Statuses
docs.text:
Status Meaning Active Full member, counts toward all reports and promotion tracking Reserve Limited participation, still on roster LOA Leave of Absence — temporarily inactive, intends to return Inactive No current participation Transferred Moved to another ship Retired Left SFI or the chapter

Tip

Use LOA for members who plan to return. Inactive is for members who have stopped participating but haven't formally left. Avoid using Retired unless the member has actually departed — it removes them from active reporting.

docs.title: Adding a Crew Member
docs.text:
Go to Crew Roster → Add Member. Required fields: SCC, full name, rank, and status. Recommended: email address and join date.

Duplicate SCCs

COMPASS won't allow two members with the same SCC on the same ship. If you get a duplicate error, check whether they're already on your roster under a slightly different name, or contact your RC if they appear on another ship.

docs.title: Editing a Crew Member
docs.text: Click any member's name to open their profile, then click Edit to update their information. From a member's profile you can also update their rank, change their status, manage department assignments, and view their promotion and awards history.

docs.title: Importing Your Roster from SFI
docs.text:
If your ship's roster in db.sfi.org has changed — new members joined, ranks updated — you can re-sync directly from the Command Dashboard.

Go to Command Dashboard → Roster Import.

Click Sync from SFI Database and enter your db.sfi.org credentials when prompted. COMPASS will fetch your latest roster, detect changes (new members, rank changes, departures), and walk you through reviewing those changes before applying the import.

If the automatic sync isn't available, use Manual Import to paste CSV data from the SFI roster export page.

Note

Credentials entered here are used once and never stored — the same as the initial ship setup.

docs.title: If your ship has been renamed
docs.text:
If db.sfi.org now uses a different name for your ship, the roster import notices and asks before changing anything:

  • It only offers a rename when at least half your current crew are on the roster. Otherwise it treats the file as another ship's roster and refuses it, as before.
  • You can adjust the capitalisation of the new name (db.sfi.org rosters often use capitals); otherwise it must match db.sfi.org.
  • Click Yes, rename and continue to rename the ship and carry on with the import. The old name stays in the ship's history. Click No, don't rename to stop without changing anything.

Crew who told COMPASS "my ship was renamed" (see Check Your Chapter) are sorted out by this import.

docs.title: Transfers
docs.text:
Members change ships themselves by updating their chapter on db.sfi.org; COMPASS follows it. There is nothing for you to approve. Members heading to your ship appear under Incoming Crew in the left navigation.

See Crew Transfers for what you see when crew arrive or leave, and when to ask your RC for a direct transfer.

docs.title: Ship Positions
docs.text:
Go to Ship Positions in the left navigation to view and manage formal position assignments (CO, XO, Department Heads, etc.).

To assign or change a position, go to Ship Positions → Manage Positions.

docs.title: Departments
docs.text:
Go to Departments in the left navigation to organise your crew into departments, assign department heads, and run department activity reports.

Crew not assigned to a department appear in the Unassigned count on the Command Dashboard.

See Departments for the full walkthrough.

docs.title: Roster Best Practices
docs.text:
• Audit monthly before submitting reports
  • Enter new members promptly — don't wait until report time
  • Use LOA for members who intend to return, not Inactive
  • Never delete members — change their status instead; historical data is preserved

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
I added a member but they can't log in. New members get a Welcome to COMPASS email with a link to set their password. The link expires after 24 hours; after that they can use Forgot password? on the login page with their SFI username. If email isn't working for them, they can click Verify with your db.sfi.org account on the login page instead. See Setting Up or Recovering Your Account.

The roster import says "Wrong ship detected!" The roster's ship name doesn't match your ship, and fewer than half your crew are on it, so COMPASS thinks it's another ship's roster. Check you exported your own chapter's roster. If your ship really was renamed and the crew is mostly the same, the import offers a rename instead (see above).

A member appears on two ships. Contact your RC to resolve. Crew can only have one active assignment at a time.

Roster import shows a member with the wrong rank. db.sfi.org is the source of truth for rank. If the rank is wrong in SFI's database, it needs to be corrected there first, then re-imported.

docs.title: Ship Settings
docs.text:
Ship Settings controls how COMPASS calculates points and promotion requirements for your ship. All settings here only affect your ship — other ships continue using their own values.

Go to Command Dashboard → Ship Settings.

docs.title: Ship Information
docs.text:
View and edit your ship's basic details — name, registry, class, region, charter city, chapter contact email, and website.

Go to Command Dashboard → Ship Information to update these.

docs.title: Event Points
docs.text:
Configure how many activity points each event type awards to attending crew.

Go to Ship Settings → Event Points to set your values. Each event type has a default SFI value shown alongside your ship's current setting. Click Set Override to customize.

Note

If your ship is using default values, point calculations automatically follow any regional defaults your RC has configured. Setting a ship-level override locks your ship to your chosen value regardless of regional changes.

docs.title: Academy Points
docs.text:
Configure point values for academy course completions by grade.

Grade Default Distinction 2 pts Honors 1 pt Pass 1 pt

Override these if your ship uses a different point scale for academy completions.

docs.title: Award Points
docs.text:
Set the permanent point values awarded when a crew member receives each award. Organized by award category (Orders of Merit, Annual Awards, Regional Awards, Ship Awards, Auxiliary Awards).

Each award shows the default SFI point value and your ship's current override. Click Set Override to customize any award's point value for your ship.

docs.title: Event Point Adjustments
docs.text:
Give your crew a starting event point balance for activity earned before your chapter joined COMPASS, or correct recording errors in bulk.
