Go to Ship Settings → Event Point Adjustments. See Opening Event Points for the full guide.

Note

Adjustments are counted inside each member's event point total, not shown separately. Entries cannot be edited or deleted — reverse one by recording the opposite amount.

docs.title: Promotion Requirements
docs.text:
Configure the point and time-in-grade requirements for each rank promotion.

For each rank, you can set:

  • Points Required — Minimum points to be eligible
  • Time in Grade — Minimum months at current rank before promotion

Warning

Changes to promotion requirements take effect immediately and recalculate all crew eligibility. Review the Promotion Eligibility Report after making changes to see the impact.

docs.title: Permanent Award Points
docs.text: Configure how permanent point bonuses are applied for specific award types and leadership positions.

docs.title: Command Action Delegation
docs.text:
Grant your XO — or, for events, OPS and SO — the authority to act on your behalf. Events, promotions, and awards each have their own set of actions you can turn on and off.

Only the CO sees this card, and grants can be revoked at any time. See Delegating Command Authority for the full guide.

docs.title: Quick Links
docs.text:
Customize the quick-action links that appear on crew member dashboards. This is how you surface the most relevant resources for your crew — your ship's website, meeting schedule, Discord server, etc.

Go to Command Dashboard → Quick Links to manage these.

docs.title: Discord Bot
docs.text:
If your ship uses a Discord server, COMPASS can sync roles, update member nicknames, and keep your Discord membership list in sync with your COMPASS roster.

Go to Command Dashboard → Discord Bot to configure the integration.

docs.title: API Tokens
docs.text:
For ships or region staff using external integrations, API tokens can be generated here.

Go to Command Dashboard → API Tokens to manage tokens.

docs.title: Withdrawing Your Ship from COMPASS
docs.text:
If your chapter decides to stop using COMPASS, the CO can withdraw the ship. This page explains what withdrawal does, what it doesn't do, and how to come back.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: What withdrawal does — and doesn't do
docs.text:
Withdrawing is about COMPASS only. Your chapter keeps operating in STARFLEET International exactly as before. Nothing changes on db.sfi.org.

When you withdraw:

  • The ship stops being tracked. It no longer appears on the Regional Dashboard or in reports.
  • Your crew become unassigned in COMPASS. Each active crew member's assignment is closed, and they get an email letting them know. Their accounts stay active, and COMPASS remembers they're waiting for your ship, so they're reconnected if it comes back.
  • Ship positions and roles end. Positions such as XO, OPS and department heads are closed, along with the access that came with them.
  • Your Regional Coordinator is notified.
  • Every record is kept. Service history, awards, promotions, events and points all stay in COMPASS.

This takes effect immediately

There's no grace period. As soon as you confirm, your crew are unassigned and the emails are on their way. If you only want to pause for a while, you don't need to withdraw — an inactive ship costs nothing.

docs.title: Who can withdraw
docs.text:
Only the Commanding Officer. The XO and other officers don't see the option.

If the CO isn't available and the chapter needs to leave COMPASS, contact your Regional Coordinator.

docs.title: How to withdraw
docs.text:
1. Go to Command Dashboard → Ship Settings.

  2. Scroll to the bottom and find Withdraw your ship from COMPASS.

  3. Click the button. The confirmation page tells you exactly how many crew members will be affected.

  4. Read the list carefully.

  5. Type your ship's name exactly as shown — capitals and spaces included. The Withdraw from COMPASS button stays greyed out until the name matches.
  6. Click Withdraw from COMPASS.

You're returned to your dashboard with a confirmation.

docs.title: Coming back
docs.text:
You can re-join COMPASS at any time:

  1. Go to the COMPASS login page and click Add Your Ship to COMPASS.
  2. Enter your ship's details as for a new ship. See Getting Started.

If your registry matches the withdrawn ship, COMPASS reactivates it rather than creating a new one. The ship is restored, the person re-joining becomes its CO, and all of its history — awards, promotions, events — is still there.

Your crew aren't restored automatically. They come back onto the ship with your next roster import. Anyone who was waiting for the ship but isn't on that roster has moved on, and stops waiting for it.

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
Will my crew lose their points or awards? No. Everything earned is kept on each member's own record and comes with them to whatever ship they join next.

Do I need to tell SFI? No. Withdrawal doesn't change anything on db.sfi.org or your chapter's standing in SFI.

What happens to our announcements and Facebook, X or Discord channels? Your chapter's announcements stay in COMPASS but nobody on the ship sees them. Nothing is posted to your channels after withdrawal.

I'm the CO and I'm leaving the chapter, but the chapter is staying. Don't withdraw. Use Leave Ship instead — see Joining or Changing Ships. Your Regional Coordinator appoints the new CO.

docs.title: Crew Member Guide
docs.text:
This guide is for crew members — anyone who is not the CO or XO of their ship. It covers what you see when you log in, how to keep track of your own service record, and how to take part in your ship's events.

About the screenshots

The screenshots in this guide come from a test copy of COMPASS. Some personal details are blurred, and the numbers on your own pages will of course be different.

docs.title: Getting Your Account
docs.text:
Usually your account is created for you: when your CO adds your ship's roster to COMPASS, you get a "Welcome to COMPASS — Your Account is Ready" email. It lists your SCC, ship, rank and username, and has a Set Your Password button.

  • The link in that email expires after 24 hours. If it has expired, use Forgot password? on the login page to get a new one.
  • No welcome email, or no access to that email address? Click Verify with your db.sfi.org account on the login page. You sign in once with your db.sfi.org account and set your COMPASS password — no email needed. See Setting Up or Recovering Your Account.
  • If your chapter isn't on COMPASS yet, you can still set up an account the same way; you'll be connected to your ship when it joins.

docs.title: Logging In
docs.text:
Go to compass.sfi.org and sign in with your username or email and your COMPASS password.

Your username is the same as on db.sfi.org, but your password is separate — changing one does not change the other.

Tick Remember me on a device you use often so you stay signed in.

Install COMPASS as an app

COMPASS can be installed on your phone or computer like an app. Go to Profile → Install COMPASS App, or use your browser's "Add to Home Screen" option. Installing it is also what lets you receive push notifications.

docs.title: Finding Your Way Around
docs.text:
The menu on the left is grouped into sections. As a crew member you will usually see:

Section Items Dashboards Crew Dashboard, Departments Operations Ship Positions, Events, and Voting if your chapter uses it Records Awards, Academy, Permanent Points Account My Record, Profile, Help / Wiki, Logout

The Notifications bell at the top of the menu shows a count when you have something new.

If you hold a position on your ship or in your region, you'll see extra items for that role. Those are covered in the Commanding Officer and Regional Coordinator guides.

docs.title: Your Dashboard
docs.text:
After logging in you land on the Crew Dashboard, a summary of where you stand.

From top to bottom:

  • Service Record — your rank (and since when), position, time in grade, time in service, training badges (OTS, OCC, SFDPP, course count) and your departments.
  • Ship Overview — active crew, events in the last 12 months, upcoming events and service hours for your ship.
  • Announcements — messages from your command team, region or the fleet.
  • Notifications — recent items for you, such as an award you received.
  • Awards & Commendations — your awards, newest first. Click Show All to see the full list.
  • Promotion Progress — your next rank and how close you are, with checks for time in grade, points and course prerequisites.
  • Points Breakdown — event and academy points, award points, permanent points and your total.
  • Your Attendance — events attended, uniforms worn, and your recent events with the points each one earned.
  • Upcoming Events — your ship's next events.
  • Quick Links — links your CO has set up, such as a reading challenge form or your ship's website.

docs.title: My Record
docs.text:
My Record (under Account) is your complete service record: ships, promotions, awards, training, events and points, with a Service Record (PDF) button for a printable copy that leaves out your personal contact details.

See My Record and Your Service Record for a tour of every section, the PDF, and how to fix details that are wrong.

docs.title: Promotion Progress
docs.text:
Your Promotion Progress card (on the dashboard and on My Record) shows the next rank you can be promoted to and three checks:

  • TIG — whether you've served enough time in your current grade
  • Points — whether you have the points the next rank requires
  • Course Prereqs — whether you've completed the required Academy courses

When all three are green you are eligible. Promotions on a ship are put forward by your command team, so if you think you're eligible, talk to your CO.

Not sure where the numbers come from? See How Promotion Points Work for the point value of every event type, academy grade, award, and permanent point award, plus the point cost and time in grade for each rank.

Not assigned to a ship?

Members without a ship request promotions themselves. See Requesting a Promotion (Unassigned).

docs.title: Events and RSVPs
docs.text:
Go to Events to see your ship's calendar. Open an event and choose Attending, Maybe or Not Attending to let your command team know whether you're coming. If an event you RSVP'd to moves or is cancelled, COMPASS tells you.

Your RSVP isn't your attendance: your command team records who attended after the event, and that's what earns points.

See Events and RSVPs for RSVPing for family members, change notices, adding your ship's calendar to your phone, and suggesting an event.

docs.title: Awards and Nominations
docs.text:
Go to Awards to see the awards you've received.

To recognise a shipmate, go to Awards → Nominate.

  1. Search for the Nominee by name or SCC. If they don't have a COMPASS account, tick Nominee is not in COMPASS.
  2. Choose an Award Type to narrow the list, then pick the Award.
  3. Write a Citation of at least 50 characters explaining why they deserve it. Add any Supporting Evidence you have.
  4. Submit. Your nomination goes to your CO for review before moving on to regional or fleet approval.

See the Awards guide for advice on writing a strong citation.

docs.title: Academy and Permanent Points
docs.text:
Academy shows SFI Academy course completions for your ship, including how many courses each member has passed with Distinction, Honors or Pass. Your own course counts also appear on My Record.

Permanent Points shows your permanent points — awards, leadership positions, OTS/OCC completions, and other sources — grouped by category.

Permanent points never reset and are never spent on a promotion. See How Promotion Points Work for the values and the per-category caps.

Why doesn't my total add up?

Each category has a cap. Points awarded above the cap are kept on your record but don't count toward your total. The bar under each category shows how much of the cap you've used; "Cap reached" means extra points in that category won't raise your total.

docs.title: Your Profile and Notifications
docs.text:
Go to Profile to manage your account.

  • SFI Identity — your name, SCC, username and membership, read only from db.sfi.org
  • Change Password — your COMPASS password
  • Email Notification Preferences and Timezone
  • Discord Notifications and Push Notifications
  • Install COMPASS App and Notification History
  • Ship Assignment — your current ship, with a Leave Ship button

See Notifications for setting up email, push and Discord notices, linking your Discord account, and using your Notification History.

docs.title: Changing Ships
docs.text:
Under SFI policy you can move to another chapter at any time. Click Leave Ship (on My Record or your Profile) to transfer to another ship, become unassigned, or move to a chapter that isn't on COMPASS. Your service history, awards, academy records, points and rank all come with you.

Your chapter is officially set on db.sfi.org, so COMPASS shows you exactly what to change there and completes your move once it sees the change.

See Joining or Changing Ships for the step-by-step walkthrough, including joining a ship when you don't have one.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
I never got a welcome email, or the link expired. Use Forgot password? on the login page with your SFI username or email. If COMPASS doesn't recognise you, ask your CO to check that you're on the ship's roster.

My rank, name or email in COMPASS is wrong. These come from db.sfi.org. Get them corrected there first; COMPASS picks up the change the next time your CO imports the roster.

My membership expiration or OTS/OCC status is out of date. Click Sync My SFI Data on My Record or your Profile.

An event I attended isn't on my record. Attendance is entered by your command team after the event, and only approved events count. If it's still missing a few days later, let your CO know.

My permanent points total is lower than the points I've been awarded. Some categories are capped — see Academy and Permanent Points.

I'm not receiving notifications. Check your Email Notification Preferences on your Profile and your spam folder. For push notifications, click Enable on this Device on each device, and make sure your browser allows notifications for compass.sfi.org.

docs.title: Joining or Changing Ships
docs.text:
Under SFI policy you can move to another chapter at any time, for any reason. This page walks through transferring to another ship, leaving your ship, and joining a ship when you don't have one.

Your history comes with you. Your service history, awards, academy records, permanent points and rank are kept whichever option you choose.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Your chapter is officially recorded on db.sfi.org, the STARFLEET member database. COMPASS follows db.sfi.org; it doesn't move you on its own say-so.

So every move has two halves:

  1. In COMPASS, you say where you're going. COMPASS then shows you exactly what to change on db.sfi.org.
  2. On db.sfi.org, you change your chapter.

As soon as COMPASS sees the change on db.sfi.org, it completes your move. Until then you stay where you are. Nothing in COMPASS changes if you never make the db.sfi.org change.

You don't need anyone's approval. The new ship's command team is told you're on your way.

docs.title: 1. Start from your ship
docs.text:
Click Leave Ship, either on My Record or at the bottom of your Profile.

Choose Transfer to another ship, optionally add a reason, and click Browse Ships.

docs.title: 2. Pick a ship
docs.text:
The ship browser lists the operating ships in your region, with their crew size. Use Region at the top right to look in another region.

Click Transfer Here on the ship you want. You can add an optional note to the new command team (a little about yourself is nice), then click Continue.

docs.title: 3. Change your chapter on db.sfi.org
docs.text:
COMPASS shows you the exact steps:

  1. Click Open Change Account Info and sign in to db.sfi.org.
  2. In the CHANGE CHAPTER list, choose the chapter COMPASS shows you, for example USS CORSAIR - R3. Use Copy if it helps you find it.
  3. Leave every other field as it is and click the SUBMIT button just below FICTIONAL SPECIES.

Family memberships

If your db.sfi.org page has an ADDITIONAL MEMBERS section further down, don't use the SUBMIT button at the bottom of that section. It adds family members and won't save your chapter.

docs.title: 4. Come back and check
docs.text:
Back in COMPASS, click I've changed it — check now. COMPASS looks you up on db.sfi.org and, if the change is there, completes your transfer straight away.

If you don't come back, that's fine: COMPASS checks overnight and finishes the transfer once db.sfi.org shows the change.

While a transfer is waiting, a banner at the top of COMPASS reminds you, with a Finish it link back to these steps.

docs.title: Leaving without joining another ship
docs.text:
From Leave Ship, choose Become unassigned, then follow the steps. On db.sfi.org you'll set your chapter to ---UNASSIGNED---.

You stay a STARFLEET member in your region, and your Regional Coordinator looks after unassigned members. You can join a ship again later.

docs.title: Moving to a chapter that isn't on COMPASS
docs.text: From Leave Ship, choose Transfer to a chapter not on COMPASS and type the chapter's name if you know it. On db.sfi.org, pick that chapter. COMPASS keeps your record, and remembers which chapter you went to: if that chapter joins COMPASS later, you're connected to it automatically when its roster is imported.

docs.title: Joining a ship when you don't have one
docs.text:
If you're unassigned, your left navigation shows Find a Ship.

  1. Click Find a Ship to open the ship browser.
  2. Click Transfer Here on the ship you want to join.
  3. Follow the db.sfi.org steps above.

docs.title: Changing your mind
docs.text:
• Pick a different ship: start again from Leave Ship or the ship browser. Choosing a new destination replaces your open request; you can only have one at a time.
  • Cancel: on the request page, click Cancel this request. Cancelling only affects COMPASS. If you already changed your chapter on db.sfi.org, change it back there too, or COMPASS will still follow it.

docs.title: Your transfer history
docs.text: On My Record, click Transfer History to see every move you've requested or made and where each one stands.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• Positions and roles end when you leave. When the move completes, your assignment on your old ship closes, along with any department assignments and ship roles there (such as CO, XO, OPS or department head).
  • If you're the CO or XO, COMPASS warns you before you leave. A ship whose CO leaves has no CO until the Regional Coordinator or an administrator appoints one; the CO appoints a new XO.
  • Your points come with you. Promotion points are counted across your whole career, not per ship.

docs.title: Check Your Chapter
docs.text: Sometimes db.sfi.org shows you on a chapter COMPASS doesn't recognise, while COMPASS has you on a ship. That usually means one of two things: you transferred to a chapter that isn't on COMPASS, or your ship has been renamed on db.sfi.org. COMPASS can't tell which, so it asks you instead of guessing.

docs.title: Where you'll see it
docs.text:
A Check your chapter banner appears at the top of your dashboard. You may also be taken straight to the question right after setting up your account.

Click Tell us what happened.

docs.title: Answering
docs.text:
Answer What happens I transferred to the new chapter You confirm on the next page, then you're removed from your COMPASS ship and its CO and XO are told. If that chapter joins COMPASS, you're connected to it automatically. My ship was renamed You stay on your ship. Your CO and XO are asked to confirm the new name; they do that with a roster import, which updates the ship's name in COMPASS. Something else is wrong You stay where you are, and your Regional Coordinator is told. Say briefly what's wrong in the box — it's required for this answer. I'm not sure You stay where you are, and your Regional Coordinator is told.

Click Continue. If you're not ready, Answer later takes you back to your dashboard; the banner stays until you answer.

docs.title: Confirming a transfer
docs.text:
Because I transferred takes you off your ship, COMPASS shows exactly what will happen before anything changes:

Click Yes, I transferred to go ahead, or Choose a different answer to go back. Your service history, awards and points are always kept.

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
The banner went away on its own. That's expected. It disappears as soon as db.sfi.org and COMPASS agree again — for example after your CO's roster import renames the ship.

I answered, but I picked the wrong option. Contact your Regional Coordinator. If you said you transferred and you hadn't, your CO's next roster import will put you back on the ship; your positions and roles will need re-assigning.

I'm the CO or XO and I said the ship was renamed. Run a roster import for your ship. It will show the new name and ask you to confirm it. See Managing Your Roster.

docs.title: Events and RSVPs
docs.text:
Your ship's events are where most of your promotion points come from. This page covers finding events, telling your command team whether you're coming, what happens when an event changes, and putting your ship's calendar on your phone.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Personal details are blurred.

docs.title: Finding events
docs.text:
Click Events in the left navigation. Switch between List and Calendar at the top right, and use Filters to narrow the list.

Your next few events also appear under Upcoming Events on your dashboard.

Open an event to see its details. Times are shown in your time zone; an all-day event shows only its date.

docs.title: RSVPing
docs.text:
Events that count for attendance have a Will you attend this event? section.

  1. Open the event.
  2. Under Your RSVP, click Attending, Maybe or Not Attending. Your choice is saved straight away and highlighted.
  3. Changed your mind? Click a different answer. You can change it until RSVP closes, 24 hours after the event starts.

Total Responses at the bottom shows how many people are attending, maybe, or not attending. The list of names is visible to your command team and to whoever created the event.

docs.title: RSVPing for your family
docs.text: If you have a family membership with SFI, your family members are listed under Family Members, each with their own buttons. RSVP for each person separately. Family groups come from the SFI roster, so if someone is missing, check the family membership on db.sfi.org.

docs.title: An RSVP is not attendance
docs.text: Your RSVP tells your command team who to expect. It doesn't earn points. After the event, your command team records who actually attended and who wore uniform, and that's what puts the points on your record. If you attended an event and it's still missing from My Record a few days later, let your CO know.

docs.title: When an event changes
docs.text:
If you RSVP'd Attending or Maybe, COMPASS tells you when the event:

  • moves — a new date or time, or switching to or from all-day
  • changes location
  • is cancelled

Renaming an event or editing its description doesn't send a notice, and nothing is sent for events that have already happened.

For a repeating event, such as a weekly meeting, a change that affects several dates you RSVP'd to arrives as one notice listing each changed date.

Notices arrive by email, push and Discord, depending on your notification settings. The Event Changes switch controls them. They're also kept in your Notification History.

Tip

If an event is cancelled, its RSVPs go with it. If it's rescheduled as a new event, RSVP again.

docs.title: Adding your ship's calendar to your phone
docs.text:
You can subscribe to your ship's events in Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook. New events appear on their own as they're approved.

  1. On the Events page, click Subscribe to Calendar.
  2. Copy the Subscription URL.
  3. Add it to your calendar app:
    • Google Calendar (on a computer): Other calendars → + → From URL, paste, then Add calendar.
    • Apple Calendar: on a Mac, File → New Calendar Subscription. On an iPhone, Settings → Calendar → Accounts → Add Account → Other → Add Subscribed Calendar.
    • Outlook: Add calendar → Subscribe from web.

Calendar apps refresh subscriptions on their own schedule, so a brand-new event can take a few hours to appear.

Note

If the window says the feed is disabled or not available yet, ask your CO or XO to turn it on in Ship Settings.

docs.title: Suggesting an event
docs.text: Crew members can create events too. Click Create Event on the Events page and fill in the form. Your event is submitted as pending and appears on the calendar once your command team approves it. See Events for what each field means.

docs.title: My Record and Your Service Record
docs.text:
My Record is your complete STARFLEET service record in COMPASS: your ships, promotions, awards, training, events and points in one place. From it you can download a printable Service Record PDF.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Some personal details are blurred.

docs.title: Opening My Record
docs.text:
Click My Record under Account in the left navigation.

You can only see your own record. Your command team and regional staff can see the records of members they oversee.

docs.title: The header
docs.text: Your name, rank, position, SCC and ship, with your Total Points at the top right. Below that is your contact information as COMPASS has it: username, email and phone. These come from db.sfi.org. To change them, see Fixing wrong details.

docs.title: Points Breakdown
docs.text:
Column What it counts Event + Academy Points Points from events you attended or hosted, plus academy courses. If points have been spent on a promotion, the amount spent is shown underneath. Award Points The point value of your awards. Permanent Points Your permanent points, after the per-category caps. Total Points What counts toward your next promotion.

See How Promotion Points Work for how each pool is earned and why event points are spent on promotion while award and permanent points are not.

docs.title: Service History
docs.text: Every ship you've served on in COMPASS, with dates, rank and status. Your current ship shows Present.

docs.title: Rank Progression
docs.text: A timeline of your promotions, oldest on the left. The first point, Start, is the rank you held before the earliest promotion COMPASS has on record. The last point is your Current rank.

docs.title: Academy Courses
docs.text: How many SFI Academy courses you've passed with Distinction, Honors and Pass. If you've beta-tested or created courses, those counts appear too.

docs.title: Recent Event Participation
docs.text: Your ten most recent events, with type, whether you wore uniform, and the points each one earned. Click View All at the bottom to see every event.

docs.title: The right-hand column
docs.text:
• Service Stats — events attended, uniform compliance (the share of events you wore uniform to), and time in service
  • Training Status — OTS, OCC and SFDPP, each with its completion date
  • Positions — your current ship and regional positions, with how long you've held them. Full History lists every position you've held.
  • Departments — the departments you belong to and your role in each
  • Membership — whether your SFI membership is active, when it expires, and how many days remain
  • Promotion Progress — your next rank and the three checks: time in grade, points, and course prerequisites
  • Events by Type — what share of your events falls into each event type
  • Current Roles — your COMPASS roles

docs.title: Downloading your Service Record PDF
docs.text:
1. Open My Record.
  2. Click Service Record (PDF) at the top right.
  3. The PDF downloads. It's usually four or five pages.

The PDF contains:

  • Your SCC, rank, chapter, region, member-since date and membership expiration
  • Promotion history, with the points each promotion used
  • Service history and position history
  • Awards and annual fleet awards
  • Training and academy
  • Event participation
  • Permanent points, item by item, with the category caps applied
  • Your promotion point totals

It deliberately leaves out your date of birth, address, phone number and email. A printed record can travel further than a web page you have to sign in to see, so it's safe to hand to a recruiter, a new chapter, or anyone else who asks for your record.

docs.title: Sync My SFI Data
docs.text:
COMPASS checks db.sfi.org on its own, but you can refresh your record yourself at any time:

  1. Click Sync My SFI Data on My Record (or on your Profile).
  2. Enter your db.sfi.org username and password.
  3. COMPASS pulls in your membership expiration, OTS and OCC completions, and academy course completions.

Your SFI password is used once for this check and is never stored.

docs.title: Fixing wrong details
docs.text: What's wrong How to fix it Name, email or phone Update it on db.sfi.org. It reaches COMPASS the next time your command team imports the roster. Rank Rank comes from promotions recorded in COMPASS and from db.sfi.org through your command team's roster import. If it's wrong, tell your CO. Membership expiration, OTS or OCC Click Sync My SFI Data. A missing event Attendance is entered by your command team after the event, and only approved events count. Ask your CO. A missing award Awards are recorded once SFI confirms them. Ask your CO if one is overdue.

docs.title: Transfer History
docs.text: Transfer History, under the buttons at the top right, lists every ship move you've requested or made, with its status. See Joining or Changing Ships.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
COMPASS can tell you when something happens that affects you: an award, a promotion decision, a change to an event you're going to, or your membership nearing expiration. You choose how you hear about it — email, Discord, push notifications on your phone, or all three — and every notice is kept in your Notification History.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: What COMPASS notifies you about
docs.text: Notice When Award Received SFI confirms an award you've received Promotion Status A promotion request involving you is approved or rejected Event Changes An event you RSVP'd Attending or Maybe to moves, changes location, or is cancelled Membership Expiring Your SFI membership is approaching its expiration date Pending Approvals Something is waiting for your review (only if you have a command or regional role)

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
Go to Profile and find Email Notification Preferences.

  1. Turn each notice On or Off with its switch.
  2. Optionally turn on the Weekly Summary Email: one email every Monday rolling up everything COMPASS told you about that week. It's sent in addition to the individual emails, not instead of them, and nothing is sent for a quiet week.
  3. Click Save Preferences.

Emails go to the address on your SFI record. To change it, update it on db.sfi.org; it reaches COMPASS the next time your command team imports the roster.

docs.title: Your time zone
docs.text: The Timezone setting in the same card controls how every date and time in COMPASS is shown to you. It starts as Use ship default — your ship's time zone. If you live somewhere else, pick your own and click Save Preferences.

docs.title: Push notifications
docs.text:
Push notifications pop up on your phone or computer even when COMPASS isn't open.

  1. Install COMPASS on the device. Go to Profile → Install COMPASS App, or use your browser's Add to Home Screen or Install option. On an iPhone or iPad this step is required — push notifications only work from the installed app.
  2. Open the installed app and go to Profile → Push Notifications.
  3. Click Enable on This Device, then Allow when your device asks.
  4. Choose which notices to receive under What to notify me about.

Push is set up per device. Repeat these steps on each phone, tablet or computer you want notified. Disable on This Device turns it off for that device only.

\"Permission denied\"

If the card says notifications are blocked, your browser or phone has refused permission for COMPASS. Allow notifications for compass.sfi.org in your browser or phone settings, then reload the page and try again.

Push reminders for Membership Expiring arrive 60, 30, 14 and 7 days before your membership expires.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text: If your chapter's Discord server has the COMPASS bot, you can get the same notices as Discord direct messages.

docs.title: Linking your Discord account
docs.text:
1. In your chapter's Discord server, type /compass link.
  2. The bot replies with a Verify My SFI Membership link. Click it.
  3. Sign in with your db.sfi.org username and password. They're used once to confirm your membership and are never stored.
  4. When it says you can close the window, go back to Discord.

Other bot commands you can use: /compass update refreshes your membership status and roles, /compass status shows your status, /compass events lists upcoming events, and /compass points shows your permanent points.

docs.title: Turning Discord DMs on or off
docs.text:
Once your account is linked, a Discord Notifications card appears on your Profile.

Switch Discord DM Notifications on or off and click Save. When it's on, you get a DM for the same notices that trigger an email.

docs.title: Notification History
docs.text:
Every notice COMPASS sends you is kept. Open it from the Notifications bell at the top of the left navigation, or Profile → Notification History → View History.

  • The heading shows how many notices you have and how many are unread.
  • Filter by type — Awards, Promotions, Events, Membership, Approvals or System — and by Unread Only, All or Read Only.
  • Click View → on a notice to go to the thing it's about.
  • Click Mark read on a single notice, or Mark All Read at the top.

The page opens showing unread notices. If it says "You're all caught up", choose All to see older ones.

docs.title: Not getting notified?
docs.text:
• No emails: check that each notice is switched On under Email Notification Preferences, and check your spam folder.
  • No push notifications: make sure COMPASS is installed on that device and push is enabled on that device. Check your phone's notification settings for COMPASS.
  • No Discord DMs: make sure your account is linked (the Discord Notifications card only appears once it is) and that Discord DM Notifications is on. Discord only delivers DMs if you share a server with the COMPASS bot and allow DMs from server members.
  • Missing event-change notices: these only go to members who RSVP'd Attending or Maybe, and not for renames or description edits. See Events and RSVPs.

docs.title: Requesting a Promotion (Unassigned Members)
docs.text:
If you are an SFI member who is not on a chapter roster in COMPASS — you are unassigned — you can ask your Regional Coordinator for a promotion yourself. Under MHB Section 02:09 the RC may promote unassigned members up to the grade of O-6.

If you are on a ship's roster, your CO handles promotions instead; this page does not apply to you.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• You must be unassigned. Your dashboard shows No Ship Assignment in the left navigation.
  • You can have one request pending at a time. If one is already waiting, the form tells you which rank it is for.
  • Promotions to O-7 and above (flag ranks) need Executive Committee approval and cannot be requested here.

docs.title: Step 1 — Open the Request Form
docs.text: On your dashboard, scroll to Quick Links and select Request Promotion.

docs.title: Step 2 — Check Your Current Standing
docs.text: The form shows your current rank and your point totals from the Academy, awards, and permanent points. Members who have never held a rank show Unranked.

docs.title: Step 3 — Choose the Rank You Are Requesting
docs.text:
COMPASS offers only the next step on your own rank track, within what an RC can approve.

When more than one rank is open to you, Requesting Promotion To is a drop-down and you choose one. When only one rank is open, it is shown on its own and there is nothing to choose.

Each option shows its grade, classification, and service:

Shown as Means Fleet The standard Starfleet enlisted and officer ladder Fleet Reserve The Crewman Recruit (CRR) enlisted track SFMC The STARFLEET Marine Corps ladder

Starting your rank track

An unranked member is offered CZN and the three E-1 entry ranks (CRMN 3C, CRR, PVT). Choosing an E-1 rank is how you choose your track. Members under 18 are also offered Cadet, and members who have completed OTS are also offered the O-1 ranks.

Once you hold a rank, the form offers the next rank on that same track. Moving sideways between tracks (for example Fleet to SFMC) is not something you can request here; talk to your RC.

docs.title: Step 4 — Add Supporting Notes and Submit
docs.text:
Supporting notes are optional but help your RC decide: Academy courses completed, events you have attended or volunteered at, community service, or anything else that supports the request.

Select Submit Promotion Request.

If your region has no RC in COMPASS

The form shows an External RC Required box asking for your RC's email address, pre-filled with your region's RC address (for example rc3@sfi.org). Your request is emailed to that RC with a secure review link, and they approve or reject it from there.

docs.title: Step 5 — Confirmation
docs.text: You return to your dashboard with a confirmation message. Your request is now waiting in your RC's queue.

docs.title: After Your RC Decides
docs.text:
• Approved — your rank updates in COMPASS and you receive a notification. Your dashboard shows the new rank and your Last Promotion.
  • Rejected — you are notified with the RC's reason, and the request leaves their queue. You can submit a new request later.

Your RC also records the promotion in the SFI member database (db.sfi.org). You do not need to do anything there yourself.

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
Why can't I choose the rank I want? The form only offers the next rank on your current track, and only up to O-6. Skipping ranks, moving to another track, and flag ranks are all decided outside this form. Ask your RC.

I joined a ship. Can I still use this? No. Once you are on a ship's roster, promotions go through your CO. A request you submitted while unassigned stays with your RC.

Can I change or withdraw a request? Contact your RC. While a request is pending you cannot submit another.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Rank Chart
  • For RCs: Approving Unassigned Member Promotions

docs.title: Setting Up or Recovering Your Account
docs.text:
You can set up your COMPASS account, or get back into it, by signing in once with your db.sfi.org account. Use this if:

  • you're new and never got a Welcome to COMPASS email, or its link has expired;
  • you've forgotten your COMPASS password;
  • your chapter isn't on COMPASS yet but you'd like an account ready for when it joins.

It works for any member whose membership on db.sfi.org is active.

docs.title: 1. Start from the login page
docs.text: On compass.sfi.org, under the sign-in form, click Verify with your db.sfi.org account.

docs.title: 2. Sign in with your db.sfi.org username and password
docs.text:
COMPASS signs in to db.sfi.org as you, once, to read your member record. It does not keep your db.sfi.org password.

If you'd like your COMPASS password to be the same as your db.sfi.org one, tick Use this same password for COMPASS. COMPASS then stores it the way it stores any COMPASS password (scrambled, never readable), and never uses it to sign in to db.sfi.org. Passwords shorter than 8 characters can't be reused; you'll be asked to choose one.

Click Verify. It takes a few seconds.

docs.title: 3. Check what COMPASS will do, then set your password
docs.text:
The next page shows your db.sfi.org record, your COMPASS username, and what will happen to your ship placement. Nothing changes until you submit this page.

If you already have an account, you're setting a new password for it:

If you ticked Use this same password for COMPASS, leave both password boxes blank and click Set password and sign in. To use a different password instead, type it in both boxes.

If you don't have an account yet, COMPASS creates one:

If db.sfi.org doesn't list a region for you, you'll also be asked to choose your region.

When you submit, you're signed in and taken to your dashboard.

You have 15 minutes

The check with db.sfi.org is good for 15 minutes. If you take longer, you'll be asked to sign in to db.sfi.org again.

docs.title: What happens to your ship
docs.text:
db.sfi.org is the official record of your chapter, so COMPASS lines your account up with it:

db.sfi.org shows you on… COMPASS… The ship COMPASS already has you on Changes nothing. A different ship that's on COMPASS Moves you there. Both ships' CO and XO are told. No chapter (unassigned) Places you with your region's unassigned members. A chapter that isn't on COMPASS yet Notes the chapter you're waiting for, and connects you automatically if it joins. A ship that has left COMPASS Notes that you're waiting for it, and reconnects you if it comes back. A chapter name COMPASS doesn't recognise, while COMPASS has you on a ship Changes nothing, and asks you what happened. See Check Your Chapter.

Every move shows in your transfer history, the same as any other transfer.

docs.title: Keeping your account safe
docs.text:
• Each time someone sets a password this way, COMPASS emails the address on your account. If you get that email and it wasn't you, change your db.sfi.org password straight away and contact your Regional Coordinator.
  • Setting a password this way signs your account out everywhere else.
  • Anyone who knows your db.sfi.org password can use this page, so keep that password private.

docs.title: Common Questions
docs.text:
It says my membership isn't active. Only active members can verify. If you've just renewed, db.sfi.org may take a day or two to show it; try again then. If you already have a COMPASS account, you can still use Forgot password? on the login page to reset by email.

It says db.sfi.org didn't accept my username and password. Check them on db.sfi.org first. After several failed tries COMPASS asks you to wait a minute before trying again.

It says my account can't be set up here. Some accounts need a person to look at them first — for example, a suspended account or one that was removed. Contact your Regional Coordinator.

Is my COMPASS username the same as my db.sfi.org username? Usually. The page shows your COMPASS username before you finish, and it's in the email COMPASS sends you.

Can I keep signing in with my db.sfi.org password every time? You sign in to COMPASS with your COMPASS username and password. If you chose to reuse your db.sfi.org password, they're the same, but changing one later doesn't change the other.

docs.title: Regional Coordinator Guide
docs.text:
This guide covers the COMPASS tools available to Regional Coordinators (RCs) and Vice Regional Coordinators (VRCs).

As RC, you have regional-level access across all ships in your region. Your COMPASS view includes a Regional Dashboard in addition to any ship-level Command Dashboard you may have as a CO.

docs.title: In This Guide
docs.text: Section What You'll Learn Regional Dashboard Monitoring region-wide ship health and what needs your attention Regional Reports Activity, service hours, crew, promotions, expirations and birthdays, with CSV exports Regional Positions Assigning your regional staff, and the access each position grants Promotions Reviewing submissions, initiating promotions, and entering external requests Awards Reviewing and approving award nominations from all ships Creating Regional Awards Setting up your region's own awards and award groups Annual Awards RAO review, choosing regional winners, and submitting to Fleet Regional and Fleet Events Creating, publishing and cancelling regional events; RSVPs and analytics Ship Lifecycle Onboarding chapters-in-training, commissioning, and ship status Chapters-in-Training The shakedown board and verifying monthly reports Unassigned Members Importing, editing, academy records, nominations and placement Unassigned Member Promotions Approving promotions for members without a ship SFI Eligibility Sync Syncing crew eligibility data from db.sfi.org

docs.title: Your Role in COMPASS
docs.text:
As RC, you are the approving authority for promotions and awards across all ships in your region. You also have visibility into ship health indicators, membership expiration, and SFDPP compliance across your entire region — not just a single ship.

Note

If you are also a CO, you will see both Command Dashboard and Regional Dashboard in your navigation. They are separate views — the Command Dashboard shows your ship only; the Regional Dashboard shows all ships in your region.

docs.title: Annual Awards (RC)
docs.text: Each year STARFLEET runs its Annual Awards — Member of the Year, Junior Member of the Year, Chapter of the Year and the rest. Nominations start in the chapters, and each region chooses one winner per category to go forward to the fleet. This page covers the region's part.

docs.title: Who does what
docs.text: Step Who Nominate Any member, and regional staff Choose each chapter's nominees The chapter's CO or XO Review nominations for the region RAO Choose the region's winners and submit them to Fleet RC, VRC Record Fleet's decision RC, VRC

docs.title: The annual awards year
docs.text: When the fleet opens Annual Awards nominations, a 🏆 Annual Awards year — Nominations Open notice appears under Attention Required on your Regional Dashboard, with the fleet's target date. Plan your region's review so your winners are submitted before then.

docs.title: Where you work
docs.text:
All of the steps below happen on Awards → Nominations, in the Annual Awards section. It has a tab for each stage you're involved in, each with a count of what's waiting:

  • My Nominations — nominations you submitted yourself.
  • RAO Review — for the RAO.
  • RC Selection — for the RC and VRC.
  • Fleet Submission — for the RC and VRC.

If more than one year has nominations, choose the year at the top.

docs.title: How nominations reach the region
docs.text:
1. Members nominate during the nomination period.
  2. Each chapter's CO or XO chooses one nomination per category for their chapter, and forwards the selected ones to the region.
  3. Forwarded nominations go to the RAO. If your region has no RAO in COMPASS, they go straight to RC Selection.

docs.title: RAO Review
docs.text:
The RAO reviews each nomination the chapters forwarded.

  • ✓ Approve — it goes on to RC Selection.
  • Reject — it goes no further. A reason is required and is kept with the nomination.

Click View Full Nomination to read the whole nomination, including the basis for the recommendation.

docs.title: RC Selection
docs.text:
The RC (or VRC) picks the region's winner in each category.

  1. Open the RC Selection tab. Approved nominations are grouped by category.
  2. Read the nominations in a category, then click ✓ Select as Winner on one. One winner per category represents your region at fleet level.

Changed your mind? Selecting a different nomination in the same category replaces your earlier choice, or click Unselect on the winner. Either way, you can only change it until you've submitted it to Fleet.

docs.title: The region award
docs.text:
Each fleet award has a regional edition, so your winner also receives the region-level award when you select them.

The nominator chose whether it should be announced straight away or held for a presentation. A held award shows ⏳ Region Award Pending — event name until it's presented. After the ceremony, click Mark Presented (here, or on Awards → Pending Presentations) to add the award to the member's record.

docs.title: Fleet Submission
docs.text:
Your winners appear on the Fleet Submission tab.

For each winner:

  • ⬇ Download PDF Form — a pre-filled Annual Award Nomination Form.
  • Open SFI Form ↗ and 📋 Copy — to submit through SFI's own form, copying the details across.
  • ✓ Mark Submitted — sends the nomination to the fleet Annual Awards Director for Executive Committee (EC) evaluation. It then shows Awaiting EC Evaluation.

View Fleet Annual Awards Dashboard shows where your submissions stand in the fleet's process.

docs.title: Recording Fleet's decision
docs.text:
When the fleet announces the results:

  • ★ Awarded — adds the fleet award to the winner's record.
  • ✗ Not Awarded — records that they weren't selected at fleet level. They keep their region award.

Fleet Decisions (Recent) at the bottom of the tab lists the outcomes you've recorded.

docs.title: If your region has no RC in COMPASS
docs.text:
When the RAO approves a nomination and there's no RC in COMPASS to select winners, COMPASS asks for the RC's email address. Enter it and click 📧 Send: the RC receives a secure link to review the nomination without a COMPASS account.

  • The nomination shows Awaiting while the link is open, and the days remaining.
  • When the RC responds, it shows ✓ Endorsed by name or ✗ Declined by name.
  • If the link expires with no response, you can Resend it, or choose Process without external RC → to continue.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Agree with your RAO how you'll compare nominations before the review starts, so each category is judged the same way.
  • Select and submit well before the fleet's target date; the EC needs time to evaluate.
  • Use the downloaded PDF to check a nomination reads well before you mark it submitted.

docs.title: Awards (RC)
docs.text: As RC, you are the approving authority for all award nominations submitted by ships in your region. This page covers the full regional awards review workflow.

docs.title: The Awards Queue
docs.text:
Go to Awards in the regional navigation to see all pending award nominations from ships in your region.

Each nomination shows the nominee, award, nominator, ship, citation, and submission date. Nominations are grouped by award category.

docs.title: Reviewing a Nomination
docs.text:
Click on any nomination to open the full review panel. The panel shows:

  • Nominator Information — name, SCC, email, and their relationship to the nominee
  • Award Information — the specific award requested and its class/level
  • Basis for Recommendation — the nominator's citation narrative
  • RC Endorsement field — your optional endorsement statement

docs.title: Adding an RC Endorsement
docs.text: For Order of Merit nominations, you can add an RC Endorsement — a brief statement from you supporting the nomination. This is included in the official submission to SFI and strengthens the case for approval. While optional, it's good practice to add one for any nomination you're forwarding.

docs.title: Submitting to SFI
docs.text:
Approving an Order of Merit does not send it to SFI

Once an Order of Merit is approved, someone has to email the form to SFI. COMPASS does not do it. The chapter CO usually sends it; you, your VRC and your RAO can too, and you all see the same reminders until it's done.

Once approved, the nomination shows a three-step checklist:

Step What to do 1. Download OoM Form (PDF) Downloads the pre-filled SFI Order of Merit nomination form 2. Email it to SFI Send the PDF to SFI MemServ - Merits Director at merit@sfi.org. Open email to merit@sfi.org starts the message with the subject filled in 3. Mark as Submitted to SFI Records the submission and clears the reminder banner for everyone in the region and the chapter

Until step 3 is done, the nomination appears in a reminder banner at the top of every page and as a red card on your dashboard. The CO guide walks through it with screenshots: Sending an Order of Merit to SFI.

When SFI replies, open the nomination and record Awarded by SFI or Rejected by SFI.

docs.title: The Pre-filled Nomination Form PDF
docs.text:
The generated PDF is pre-filled with all nominee, nominator, region, and chapter information — eliminating most of the manual data entry on the SFI side.

Review the PDF before submitting to confirm all details are correct. If anything needs correcting, return to the nomination and edit before downloading again.

docs.title: Notification Preferences
docs.text:
When approving award nominations, set the Notification Preference for how and when the member is told about their award:

Option When to Use Notify immediately Member can be told right away Hold until presented You plan to present the award at a meeting, event, or convention and want to announce it in person first

This setting is per nomination — you can hold some awards and immediately notify others based on the circumstances.

docs.title: Awards Workflow Tips
docs.text:
• Check Attention Required on your Regional Dashboard daily — the Award Nominations and Annual Award Nominations tiles count everything waiting for regional action, alongside pending promotions
  • Always add an RC Endorsement for Order of Merit nominations — it strengthens the submission and signals to SFI that the nomination has regional backing
  • Use Hold until presented for awards you plan to announce at the Regional Summit or ship events — it makes for a better experience for the recipient
  • Encourage COs to write detailed citation narratives — vague citations slow down SFI processing and reflect poorly on the submission
  • Click Mark as Submitted to SFI as soon as the form is emailed to merit@sfi.org — it clears the reminder for the CO and the rest of regional staff, and stops a second person emailing the same nomination

docs.title: Chapters-in-Training
docs.text:
The Chapters-in-Training board tracks every chapter in your region that is in shakedown: how far through it is, whether it's keeping up with monthly reporting, and whether it's ready to commission.

How chapters get onto the board, and how they leave it, is covered in Ship Lifecycle.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Names are blurred.

docs.title: Who can see it
docs.text: The RC, VRC and RSHOO, plus fleet shakedown officers. Fleet officers get a Fleet view selector to look at any region.

docs.title: The board
docs.text:
Go to Regional Dashboard → Regional Actions → Chapters-in-Training, or Regional Reports → Chapters-in-Training.

Each chapter in shakedown gets a card:

Field What it shows Progress How far through shakedown the chapter is, as a percentage and a bar. Month Which month of the 9-month START Manual it's in. Started / Target The launch date and the target commission date (earlier if the chapter qualified for the Accelerated Shakedown Program). Crew Active crew against the 10 needed to commission. Reporting How many of the monthly report items due so far are done and verified. Green at 100%, yellow from 75%, red below. XO OCC Due The XO's OCC deadline (60 days from launch). Red once it has passed.

A red note under the bar flags anything outstanding, such as a monthly report item.

Each card has View Checklist and Commission buttons.

docs.title: A chapter's shakedown page
docs.text:
Click View Checklist to open a chapter's shakedown page.

  • Totals — months in shakedown, active crew (out of 10), target commission date, and progress.
  • Timeline — launch date (with Change), minimum commission date and target date.
  • Command Staff — the CO and XO, with the XO's OCC due date (marked OVERDUE once it passes).
  • Launch Requirements — what had to be in place at launch. Most are auto-verified by COMPASS; any that aren't can be marked done here.
  • Status History and Support Ship (with Change).
  • Monthly Checklist — see below.

docs.title: Verifying monthly reports
docs.text:
Each month of shakedown has a checklist from the STARFLEET START Manual. The chapter's command team marks items done as they complete them. Your job is to check and verify them.

Items can be verified by the RC or RSHOO for chapters in their region, and by the support ship's command team for the chapters they mentor. A chapter can never verify its own items.

  1. Open the chapter's shakedown page and scroll to Monthly Checklist.
  2. Open the current month (or an earlier one).
  3. For each item the chapter has marked done, check it against what you've received, then verify it.

A required reporting item only counts once it's both done and verified. Those items feed the commission checklist, so an unverified month holds the chapter back even if the chapter did the work. The other items are acknowledgments that are simply tracked.

Tip

Verify monthly items as reports come in rather than saving them up. A chapter that is up to date shows 100% Reporting on the board, and it's obvious at a glance which chapters need a nudge.

docs.title: When a chapter is ready
docs.text: When the minimum period has passed, crew is at 10 or more, the XO has OCC, and reporting is complete, click Commission on the card. See Commissioning a chapter.

docs.title: Regional and Fleet Events
docs.text:
Regional events are events you run for the whole region: a summit, a regional convention table, a virtual game night. Chapters add your event to their own calendars, their crew RSVP and get attendance credit there, and you see the turnout across the region.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text:
Task Who Create, edit, cancel and delete regional events RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO See RSVPs for your region's events RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO Add a regional or fleet event to a ship's calendar CO, XO, OPS, SO

Fleet-wide events work the same way, under the Fleet Events tab. They're created at fleet level by a COMPASS administrator.

docs.title: The Regional Events page
docs.text:
Go to Events → Shared Regional/Fleet Events, or Regional Dashboard → Regional Actions → Regional Events.

The page has three sets of controls:

  • Regional Events / Fleet Events — which scope you're looking at.
  • Official / Shared by Chapters — events created by regional or fleet staff, or events individual chapters have shared with the region. See Sharing Events Between Chapters for the chapter side.
  • Analytics — participation statistics (see below).

It lists upcoming events, plus any from the last 24 hours.

docs.title: Creating an event
docs.text:
1. Click Create Region Event.

  2. Fill in the form:

    • Event Title and Description
    • Event Date & Time, and the Event Timezone that time is in. Each attendee sees it converted to their own time zone.
    • End Date & Time — optional; uses the same time zone.
    • Location — a place, or Discord, Online and so on.
    • Event Type — this sets the points chapters' crew earn for attending.
    • Region — your region.
  3. Click Create Event.

New events start as a Draft. Chapters can't see a draft. When it's ready, open the event, click Edit, set the Status to Published, and save.

docs.title: How chapters take part
docs.text:
Once an event is published, it appears on every chapter's Shared Regional/Fleet Events page. A ship's CO, XO, OPS or SO adds it to their calendar, which creates a copy on that ship:

  • the chapter's crew RSVP on their ship's copy;
  • attendance is recorded on the copy, so the points go to their own record;
  • you see the combined turnout on your event.

The event page shows Expected Attendance — how many people are attending across how many ships and regions. Chapters only share counts with you, never individual names.

docs.title: Seeing RSVPs
docs.text:
On the event page, click View RSVPs. You'll see:

  • totals for Attending, Maybe, Not Attending and Total Expected, including any external attendees expected;
  • Participation by Ship — each chapter's attending, maybe and not attending counts;
  • Individual Responses for your region.

docs.title: Changing or cancelling an event
docs.text:
• Edit — change any detail, or its status.
  • Cancel Event — opens a confirmation page showing which ships have the event on their calendar, how many confirmed attendees are affected, and the RSVP summary. Click Cancel Event to confirm. This sets the event to Cancelled, cancels it on every ship's calendar, and notifies everyone who RSVP'd. It can't be undone.
  • Delete — removes an event entirely. Use Cancel instead for an event chapters have already added, so their crew are told.

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text:
Click Analytics on the Regional Events page for participation across your events.

  • Switch between Regional and Fleet, and filter by region.
  • Totals — total events, total attending, external guests, ships participating and attendance rate.
  • Participation by Ship and Participation by Region — attending, maybe and not attending for each.
  • Recent Events — each event with its attendance.

Use it to see which chapters turn out for regional events and which you might reach out to.

docs.title: Regional Positions
docs.text:
Regional positions record who holds each job on your regional staff — RC, VRC, Chief of Staff, Awards Officer and so on. Assigning someone a position also gives them the COMPASS access that goes with it.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Names are blurred.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Task Who See your region's positions Regional staff Assign and remove holders, edit dates RC, VRC Add, switch on/off, edit or delete positions RC, VRC

docs.title: Your regional staff
docs.text:
Go to Regional Dashboard → Regional Actions → Set Regional Positions.

The heading shows how many positions are filled and how many are vacant. Positions are grouped by department, such as Command and Operations. Each row shows the abbreviation, the position, who holds it, since when, and for how long.

docs.title: Assigning someone
docs.text:
1. Click Assign on a vacant position, or on a position that allows more than one holder.
  2. Search for the member and pick them.
  3. Set the start date, then confirm.

docs.title: Changing or ending an assignment
docs.text:
• Edit Dates — correct when someone started (or ended) in the position.
  • Remove — end their time in the position. Their history is kept, so they appear in the position's record and on their own crew record.

docs.title: What an assignment does
docs.text:
Assigning a position does more than fill in a name:

  • It grants the linked role. Each position is linked to a COMPASS role — the RAO position grants the Regional Awards Officer role, and so on. The new holder gets that role's access straight away.
  • It awards leadership points. Regional leadership positions count toward the member's permanent points under Leadership Positions.
  • Removing it takes the role away — unless the member holds another position that grants the same role.

Tip

Because positions grant access, keep them up to date. When someone steps down, Remove them on the day so their access ends too.

docs.title: Setting up positions
docs.text: Click Manage at the top of the Regional Positions page.

docs.title: Standard positions
docs.text:
Every region has the same standard positions: RC, VRC, RCOS, RAO, RDL, RSHOO, RCOO, RCOC and the others. You can't delete these, but you can:

  • switch a position off if your region doesn't use it (the RC position is always on);
  • Edit its description, for example to explain how your region divides the VRC role between north and south.

docs.title: Custom positions
docs.text:
Under Custom Positions, click Add Custom Position to create a job your region needs that isn't in the standard list, such as a second VRC or an Acting RC.

  • Position Name and Abbreviation
  • Department — the group it appears under
  • Linked Role — the COMPASS role holders receive, or None for a title with no extra access
  • Max Holders — how many people can hold it at once
  • Description

Custom positions can be switched on and off, edited, and deleted.

Warning

Choose the Linked Role carefully. Linking a custom position to a role gives everyone you assign to it that role's full access.

docs.title: Promotions (RC)
docs.text: As RC, you are the approving authority for all promotion submissions from ships in your region. This page covers the full regional review workflow for both standard and flag officer promotions.

docs.title: How Submissions Reach You
docs.text: When a CO submits a promotion in COMPASS, the member's row on their Promotion Eligibility Report changes to show Submitted for Approval with a Pending badge. The submission simultaneously appears in your Regional Promotions queue.

docs.title: The Regional Promotions Page
docs.text:
Go to Regional Promotions in the left navigation (visible only with an RC-level role) to see all pending submissions across your region.

The page is divided into three sections:

Section Contents O6 & Below Pending Approval Promotions awaiting your direct approval: Captain promotions from ships, and unassigned members' own requests (see Approving Unassigned Member Promotions) O-7+ Pending Recommendation Fleet Captain and above awaiting your recommendation to SFI Fleet Command Recently Actioned All promotions you've recently approved, rejected, or forwarded — with current status

Each row shows the member, ship, from/to rank, submitted by, submitted date, CO Recommendation status, and a Review button.

docs.title: Reviewing an O-6 Promotion (Captain)
docs.text:
Click Review on any O-6 submission to open the review panel.

The panel shows:

  • Member and ship details — name, ship, from/to rank, points, promotion date, submitted by
  • CO Recommendation — green badge if the CO recommends approval
  • Nomination Form Answers — the CO's narrative responses to all promotion questions

You can edit individual answers inline by clicking Edit on any question before approving — useful for correcting typos or clarifying answers before the record is finalised.

docs.title: Approving
docs.text: Click Approve Promotion. The member's rank updates in COMPASS immediately and they receive an email notification. The promotion moves to Recently Actioned with an Approved status badge.

docs.title: Rejecting
docs.text: Click Reject Promotion and provide a reason. The CO receives the rejection with your reason. The promotion is removed from the queue and the CO can correct and resubmit.

docs.title: Reviewing an O-7+ Promotion (Fleet Captain and above)
docs.text:
O-7+ promotions cannot be approved at the regional level — your role is to review, endorse, and forward to SFI Fleet Command. Click Review on any O-7+ submission.

Review the full submission including all nomination form answers. Edit any answers inline if needed.

You have three options:

Button Action Recommend to Fleet Forwards the nomination to SFI Fleet Command with optional endorsement notes Nomination Form Downloads the pre-filled Flag Promotion Nomination Form PDF Reject Rejects at the regional level — CO is notified with your reason

docs.title: Downloading the Nomination Form PDF
docs.text:
Before forwarding, download and review the generated PDF using the Nomination Form button. COMPASS pre-fills the entire form from data already in the system.

The PDF includes nominee details, current/requested rank, all positions held since last rank date, OTS/OCC/SFDPP completion dates, and the CO's narrative recommendation answers. Review it carefully — this is the document SFI Membership Services receives.

docs.title: Recommending to Fleet
docs.text:
Click Recommend to Fleet. A confirmation dialog appears where you can add optional notes to Fleet Command.

Click Recommend to Fleet to confirm. COMPASS returns to the Regional Promotions page with a confirmation banner.

docs.title: After Recommending — Awaiting Fleet Decision
docs.text:
After forwarding, the promotion moves to the Recently Actioned table with a status of Awaiting Fleet Decision. Two action buttons remain available.

Note

The external approval process now continues outside COMPASS. SFI Fleet Command will review the nomination and respond to you directly. Submit the PDF to SFI Membership Services per the standard process if you haven't already.

docs.title: Recording the Fleet Decision
docs.text:
When SFI Fleet Command responds, return to the Regional Promotions page and click Record Fleet Decision on the promotion row.

Select Approved or Rejected, add any notes from Fleet Command, and click Submit Decision.

If approved, the member's rank updates in COMPASS immediately and they receive an email notification. The promotion status changes to Approved in the Recently Actioned table.

docs.title: Initiating a Promotion
docs.text:
You don't have to wait for a CO to submit. The RC, VRC and RCOS can put a member forward themselves — for example, to recognise regional service, or to start a Flag nomination.

  1. On the Regional Promotions page, click + Initiate Promotion / Flag Nomination.

  2. Under Nominee, search for the member by name or SCC. You can choose anyone in your region, including unassigned members.

  3. Choose the Requested Rank and Effective Date, and give the Reason for Promotion. The reason is shown to the member's CO if the promotion goes to them.
  4. Read the routing note COMPASS shows once you've chosen a nominee and rank, and the advisory Eligibility check (points, time in grade, course prerequisites).
  5. Fill in what the route asks for (below), and optionally the Nomination Form Questions.
  6. Click Initiate.

docs.title: How it's routed
docs.text:
COMPASS picks the route from the requested rank and the member's situation:

Promotion What happens O-5 and below, chapter member Goes to the member's CO to confirm the chapter requirements (points, time in grade) and approve or decline. O-5 and below, member is their chapter's CO Skips the CO step — there's no one above them in the chapter — and you apply it directly. O-5 and below, unassigned member You apply it directly. O-6 (Captain/Colonel) You apply it directly. The CO's input is optional and advisory; a CO can't veto it. O-7 and above Creates a Flag nomination packet for Fleet/EC review. The rank doesn't change until Fleet decides. An RC Recommendation Letter is required.

For O-6 and Flag nominations you can tick Chapter CO Input (Advisory) to ask the member's CO for examples of their chapter accomplishments (Question 3 of the nomination form). It's advisory only: you can apply or submit at any time, and doing so withdraws the request.

You can't initiate a promotion for yourself, or for a member outside your region.

docs.title: Entering an External Promotion
docs.text:
Some promotion requests arrive outside COMPASS — through the SFI website, on a paper form, or from a chapter that doesn't use COMPASS. Enter them so they go through the same regional workflow and are tracked with everything else.

The RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO and RAO can enter them.

  1. On the Regional Promotions page, click + Enter External Request.

  2. Optional: if you have a filled-in STARFLEET Flag Promotion Nomination Form PDF, choose it under Import from Nomination Form PDF and click Import PDF. COMPASS fills in the form from it and shows you everything it extracted. Check every field before going on.

  3. Under Member Information, choose:
    • COMPASS Member — search by name or SCC; or
    • Non-COMPASS Member (Manual Entry) — type their full name, SCC, email, chapter and region.
  4. Under Promotion Details, set the current rank (or let COMPASS detect it), the Requested Rank, the Promotion Date, and the CO Recommendation if there is one (Recommends Approval or Not Recommended). Add notes and any nomination-form details you have.
  5. Submit.

The Workflow Status is set from the requested rank: O-6 and below land in your queue as Pending RC Approval; O-7 and above as Pending RC Recommendation. From there, review them like any other submission.

docs.title: Promotion Workflow Tips
docs.text:
• Check Attention Required on your Regional Dashboard daily — its Pending Promotions tile counts every O-6+ promotion waiting for you across all ships
  • Make sure OTS/OCC data is current before you decide. Open the member's record (Regional Dashboard → the ship's Roster → the member) and click Sync SFI Data, or ask the CO to run a full SFI Eligibility Sync for the ship
  • Download and review the Flag Promotion PDF before forwarding to Fleet — easier to catch data issues in the PDF view than in the form
  • Edit nomination narrative answers inline before approving if the CO's responses are vague — stronger narratives mean faster SFI processing
  • For O-7+ promotions, record the Fleet decision in COMPASS as soon as you hear back — it keeps your Recently Actioned table accurate and notifies the member promptly

docs.title: Creating Regional Awards
docs.text:
Regional awards are your region's own commendations — a Region Commendation, a Purple Heart, a chapter-of-the-year award. Once you create one, every chapter in your region can nominate crew (or chapters) for it.

This page covers setting awards up. Reviewing the nominations that come in is covered in Awards (RC).

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Task Who Create regional awards and award groups RC, VRC, RAO, RCOS, RCOO Edit awards and groups RC, VRC, RAO Deactivate, delete, or delete groups RC, VRC, RAO

docs.title: Your regional awards
docs.text:
Go to Regional Dashboard → Regional Actions → Manage Regional Awards.

Each award shows its group, name, recommended points, approval level, status and description. From here you can Edit, Deactivate or Delete an award.

docs.title: Creating an award
docs.text:
1. Click + Create Regional Award.

  2. Fill in the form:

    • Award Name
    • Award Scope — Individual (given to a crew member) or Chapter (given to a ship).
    • Recommended Points — the promotion points the award is worth. Ships can override this value for their own crew.
    • Group and Sort Order — where it appears in award lists (see Award groups). Lower sort orders come first.
    • Approval Level:
      • Chapter — the CO approves nominations directly. Use this for awards chapters can give on their own judgement.
      • Regional — the CO recommends, then the RAO or RC approves. Use this for awards the region wants to decide.
    • Description and Eligibility Criteria — what the award is for and who qualifies. Chapters see this when nominating, so be specific.
  3. Click Create Regional Award.

The award is active straight away, and chapters in your region can nominate for it.

docs.title: Changing an award
docs.text:
• Edit — change any of the fields above.
  • Deactivate — retires the award. Nobody can be nominated for it any more, but everyone who has received it keeps it. You can reactivate it later.
  • Delete — removes the award permanently. You can't delete an award with pending nominations; deactivate it instead. Members who have already received it keep the award on their record.

Tip

Prefer Deactivate over Delete. It keeps the award's history intact and can be undone.

docs.title: Award groups
docs.text:
Groups organise your awards into sections, such as Individual Awards and Chapter Awards. Click Manage Groups on the Regional Awards page.

  • Add Group — enter a name and an order.
  • Use the ▲ and ▼ arrows to reorder groups.
  • Rename a group and click Save.
  • Switch a group Active or Inactive.
  • Delete a group — its awards become ungrouped; they aren't deleted.

Groups appear in the order you set. Within a group, awards sort by their own sort order, then alphabetically. Ungrouped awards are listed after all groups.

Groups belong to your region. Ships keep their own groups separately, and groups aren't shared between regions.

docs.title: Regional Dashboard
docs.text:
The Regional Dashboard is your view of every chapter in your region: what needs your attention, how each ship is doing, and shortcuts to the regional tools.

Go to Regional Dashboard under Dashboards in the left navigation. It appears for regional staff (RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO, RAO and RCOC) and for fleet officers who oversee regions.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Member names are blurred.

docs.title: Header and Summary
docs.text:
The top of the page shows your region's name, the states it covers, and your regional role.

Fleet officers

If your role covers more than one region, a region selector appears beside the heading. Pick a region to switch the whole dashboard to it.

docs.title: Attention Required
docs.text:
This panel appears only when something needs action, with a badge showing the total count. Each tile links to where you deal with it:

Tile What it means Pending Promotions O-6 and above promotions waiting for RC action. Opens Regional Promotions. Ship Join Requests Established chapters asking to join COMPASS. Award Nominations Nominations waiting for regional action. See Awards. Annual Award Nominations Annual award nominations waiting for your regional selection. Expired Memberships Crew across your region whose SFI membership has expired. Opens the regional crew report. Inactive Ships Operating ships with no events in the last 60 days.

While an Annual Awards cycle is open, a Nominations Open notice also appears here, with the fleet's target date.

docs.title: Summary bar
docs.text:
Four totals for the region:

  • Active Ships — chapters that are operating, including chapters-in-training (shakedown)
  • Total Personnel — active crew on those ships. Crew of chapters-in-training are not counted here, even though their ships are counted under Active Ships.
  • Events (30 Days) — events held in the last 30 days
  • Unassigned Members — members in your region with no ship. Click it to open the unassigned members dashboard. A "+ n pending ship" line counts unassigned members attached to a ship that is still being set up in COMPASS.

docs.title: Fleet Status
docs.text:
Every active ship in your region gets a card, largest crew first. Each card shows:

  • Crew, Events/30d, Upcoming events, and Expired memberships
  • The CO and XO (or "Vacant"), and how long it has been since the ship's last event
  • Links to that ship's Roster, Events and Positions, plus Status if you can manage ship status
  • A pending count if the ship has events waiting for approval

docs.title: Health indicator
docs.text:
The coloured dot in each card's corner is a quick health check. COMPASS counts three warning signs:

  1. One or more crew have an expired membership
  2. No events in the last 60 days (or no events at all)
  3. Fewer than 5 active crew
Indicator Warning signs 🟢 Healthy None 🟡 Attention One 🔴 Critical Two or more

The indicator is a prompt for a conversation with the CO, not a judgement. A small chapter that meets regularly can show "Attention" simply because it has fewer than five members.

docs.title: Non-Operational Ships
docs.text: Ships that are dry-docked, in reserve, decommissioned or otherwise not operating don't get a card.
