If your region has any, a Non-Operational Ships button appears below Fleet Status with a count. It opens a list of those ships and their status, with a Manage Status link for officers who can change it.

docs.title: Region Overview
docs.text:
A chart with two tabs:

  • Crew Distribution — active crew on each ship
  • Events (90 Days) — events each ship has held in the last 90 days

docs.title: Regional Actions
docs.text:
Shortcuts to the regional tools. Which ones you see depends on your role.

Link Use it to Regional Promotions Review O-6 and above promotion requests. See Promotions (RC). Regional Reports Run cross-ship reports for the region. Set Regional Positions Assign the RC, VRC and regional staff positions. Unassigned Members Manage members in your region with no ship. See Unassigned Member Promotions. Chapters-in-Training Manage shakedown chapters and onboarding. Ship Join Requests Review established ships asking to join COMPASS. Regional Awards Review award nominations. See Awards (RC). Regional Events View and manage regional events. SFDPP Training Track crew privacy training compliance. Manage Regional Awards Create and manage awards specific to your region.

A badge on a link shows how many items are waiting there.

docs.title: Regional Announcements
docs.text: Active announcements for your region are listed here. Officers who can post announcements see a Manage Announcements button to create or edit them.

docs.title: Recent Activity
docs.text: The five most recent promotions in your region, followed by the eight most recent events, with the ship each belongs to.

docs.title: If You're Also a CO
docs.text:
When you hold both a ship role (CO or XO) and a regional role, the left navigation shows both Command Dashboard and Regional Dashboard:

  • Command Dashboard — your own ship only
  • Regional Dashboard — every ship in your region

You can move between them freely.

docs.title: Regional Reports
docs.text:
Regional reports pull together figures from every chapter in your region. Each one can be narrowed to a single ship, and four of them export to CSV for spreadsheets or your own reporting.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS.

docs.title: Who can see them
docs.text:
Task Who View regional reports RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO, RAO, RCOC, RSHOO, RDL and RSS Export to CSV RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO and RAO

Every report covers your own region. Fleet officers who oversee several regions can choose which region to view.

docs.title: Opening the reports
docs.text:
Go to Regional Dashboard → Regional Actions → Regional Reports.

Every report has a Ship filter at the top. Leave it on All Ships (Region) for the whole region, or pick one chapter. Where a report has an Export CSV button, the export uses the same filters you've chosen.

docs.title: Activity Summary
docs.text:
Events, attendance and uniform compliance across the region.

  • Time Period — the last 30 days, 3 months, 6 months, year, 5 years, or all time.
  • Totals — total events, total attendance, and average attendance per event.
  • Charts — events by type, attendance by event type, an event timeline, and events by ship.
  • Most Attended Events — ranked by the percentage of each ship's crew who attended, so a small chapter's well-attended meeting ranks fairly against a large chapter's.
  • Event Type Details — how many of each event type, and their average attendance.

Export CSV downloads the region's totals for the period, then one row per chapter: events, total attendance, average attendance and uniform compliance.

docs.title: Service Hours
docs.text:
Community-service hours logged by your chapters.

  • Time Period — the same choices as the Activity Summary.
  • Charts — total hours by ship, hours by service type, and a timeline.
  • Top Volunteers — the members with the most hours, with their ship and event count.
  • Recent Service Events — each event with its hours, participants and location.
  • Ship Statistics — total hours, contributors and events for each ship.

Export CSV downloads one row per chapter for the period: total hours, contributors, events, active crew and average hours per member.

docs.title: Crew Status
docs.text:
The make-up of your region's crew.

  • Totals — total personnel, active ships, officers, enlisted and cadets.
  • Crew Distribution by Ship — a chart of crew per chapter.
  • Ship Statistics — for each ship: personnel, officers, enlisted, cadets, and OTS and OCC completion rates. OTS is green at 75% and above, yellow from 50%; OCC is green at 50% and above, yellow from 25%.

docs.title: Promotion Pipeline
docs.text:
How promotions are moving through the region.

  • Totals — pending promotions, promotions in the last 90 days, and average days in rank.
  • Pending Promotions by Ship — a chart.
  • Ship Statistics — for each ship: pending promotions, promotions in the last 90 days, average time in rank, and promotion velocity (promotions per month).

docs.title: Membership Expirations
docs.text:
Lapsed and soon-to-lapse SFI memberships across every chapter.

  • Totals — crew with an expiration date on file, already expired, and expiring in the next 30 and 60 days.
  • Expirations by Threshold — a chart grouping members from expired through 60 days out.
  • Expirations by Ship — each chapter's expired count, percentage expired, and expiring in the next 30 days, sorted with the chapters carrying the most lapsed memberships at the top.
  • Member lists — each member's SCC, name, rank, position, ship, expiration date and days remaining (or days since it lapsed).

Export CSV downloads the member list for the ship you've selected. Use it to plan renewal reminders with your COs.

docs.title: Birthday Report
docs.text:
Upcoming crew birthdays across the region, for cards, shout-outs or newsletters.

  • Totals — crew with a birthday on file, birthdays today, this week (0–7 days) and this month (0–30 days).
  • Charts — birthdays by month and by ship.
  • Lists — today's birthdays and the week ahead, with each member's ship and the age they're turning.

Export CSV downloads the birthday list for the ship you've selected.

Personal information

The expirations and birthday exports contain members' names, SCCs and dates. Keep them to regional business, and don't post them anywhere public.

docs.title: Chapters-in-Training
docs.text: The Reports page also links to the Chapters-in-Training board, which tracks shakedown progress and monthly reporting. See Chapters-in-Training.

docs.title: SFI Eligibility Sync
docs.text:
The SFI Eligibility Sync pulls current membership status, OTS/OCC completions, academy records, and SFI affiliations directly from db.sfi.org for every crew member on a ship. This keeps COMPASS promotion eligibility calculations accurate without requiring manual data entry.

Go to Command Dashboard → SFI Database Sync to sync your own ship.

Other ships in your region

The Regional Dashboard doesn't link to other ships' sync pages. To sync one member on another ship, open their record (Regional Dashboard → the ship's Roster → the member) and click Sync SFI Data. A full-ship sync for another chapter is run by that ship's CO or XO.

docs.title: What Gets Synced
docs.text:
Each sync pulls the following from db.sfi.org for every crew member:

Field Description SFI Status Active, expired, or suspended membership status OTS Officer Training School completion OCC Officer Candidate Course completion SFDPP Privacy training compliance status Courses Academy course completions and grades Affiliations SFI chapter affiliations on record

The SFI Eligibility Overview shows a summary count across all these fields for the ship.

docs.title: Running a Sync
docs.text:
From the SFI Eligibility Overview page, click Sync All Crew in the top right corner.

Enter your db.sfi.org credentials when prompted and click Login & Sync. COMPASS will authenticate against db.sfi.org and begin pulling eligibility data for each crew member.

The sync runs crew by crew and shows real-time progress. When complete, a summary banner shows how many records were synced, skipped, or failed.

A result of "X synced, 0 failed, Y skipped" is normal — skipped means the member's data was already up to date and no changes were needed.

docs.title: Reading the Eligibility Overview
docs.text:
The overview table shows each crew member with columns for:

Column Meaning SCC Member number Status SFI membership status (Active/Expired) OTS ✓ if completed, ✗ if not OCC ✓ if completed, ✗ if not SFDPP ✓ current, ⚠ expiring, ✗ not completed Courses Count of academy courses completed Affiliations SFI chapter affiliations on file Synced How recently data was pulled from db.sfi.org

Members with warnings or missing requirements will stand out visually — use this view to identify who needs to complete training before their next promotion.

docs.title: How Often to Sync
docs.text:
Run a sync at least monthly — ideally before processing any promotions or submitting regional reports. Since OTS and OCC completions in db.sfi.org are what gate officer promotions, stale data here is the most common cause of "member shows ineligible but should qualify" issues.

Tip

If a crew member just completed OTS or OCC, run an individual sync for that member immediately rather than waiting for the monthly sync. The sync is fast for a single member.

docs.title: Individual Member Sync
docs.text: To sync a single crew member rather than the whole ship, click the sync icon in the Actions column next to their row on the eligibility overview page. This is faster for spot-checking after a member completes training.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Sync failed for a specific member. The most common cause is a SCC mismatch — the SCC in COMPASS doesn't match what's on file in db.sfi.org. Check the member's profile and correct the SCC, then retry.

Member shows OTS incomplete but they finished it. Run an individual sync for that member to pull the latest data. If it still shows incomplete after syncing, the completion may not yet be recorded in db.sfi.org — the member should contact their academy administrator.

Sync completed but SFDPP still shows expired. SFDPP expiration is date-based. If the member completed recertification recently, confirm the completion date in db.sfi.org and sync again.

docs.title: Ship Lifecycle
docs.text:
This page covers a chapter's life in COMPASS from the regional side: launching a new chapter-in-training, guiding it through shakedown, commissioning it, and changing a chapter's status later on.

Day-to-day tracking of chapters in shakedown is on the Chapters-in-Training board.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Names are blurred.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Task Who Onboard a new chapter-in-training RC, RSHOO Change a launch date or support ship; convert a chapter to shakedown RC, VRC, RSHOO Commission a chapter RC Change a chapter's operational status RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO

docs.title: The stages
docs.text: Stage Registry What it means Shakedown (chapter-in-training) NX-##### A new chapter working through the START Manual, normally for 9 months, with a commissioned support ship as mentor. Deployed NCC-##### A commissioned, fully operating chapter. Stand-By, Dry-Docked, Restricted, Reserve NCC-##### Commissioned chapters in a reduced or limited state. See Operational status. Decommissioned — Formally closed.

docs.title: Onboarding a new chapter-in-training
docs.text:
Go to Chapters-in-Training → + Onboard New Chapter (from the Regional Dashboard's Chapters-in-Training action).

The wizard has four steps.

docs.title: 1. Vessel Details
docs.text:
• Chapter Name, Shakedown Registry (NX-##### format) and Ship Class.
  • City / Location of Charter — optional, and it can't be changed after launch.
  • Support Ship — the commissioned chapter mentoring this one. Its CO co-signs the VRR, and the handbook recommends it has been commissioned for at least 12 months; COMPASS warns you if it hasn't. Only fully deployed chapters can be chosen.
    • If the support ship isn't on COMPASS, leave this blank and track the mentorship outside COMPASS. You can set it later.
    • Tick Show chapters from other regions for a support ship in another region. That's uncommon and needs both Regional Coordinators' approval on the VRRs.

The page also reminds you which offices to involve: DTS must approve the name, class and registry before the VRR; OTI can advise on established ship classes; ASDB handles original designs and needs 2–3 months' notice.

docs.title: 2. Command Staff
docs.text: Search for the members who will be CO and XO, and pick each one. Both must be current STARFLEET members, and the search results show each person's SFDPP status.

docs.title: 3. Requirements
docs.text:
COMPASS checks each officer against the launch requirements:

  • CO — OTS, OCC and current SFDPP completed.
  • XO — OTS and current SFDPP completed. OCC isn't required before launch; the XO has 60 days from launch to complete it, and COMPASS tracks the deadline.
  • Both officers are 18 or older.

Then complete the administrative items:

  • DTS Approval — record the approval reference (email date, ticket number and so on).
  • Accelerated Shakedown Program (ASP) — tick each ASP criterion the chapter meets. Standard shakedown is 9 months. Each criterion takes 1 week off, up to 8 weeks, but shakedown is never shorter than 7 months.
  • RC Notes — anything you want on record.

docs.title: 4. Review & Launch
docs.text:
Check the summary: vessel, command staff, support ship, shakedown timeline (launch date, XO OCC due date, minimum commission date) and checklist. Unchecked items are listed. You can still launch, but resolve them before the chapter's first monthly report.

Tick the confirmation and click 🚀 Launch Chapter-in-Training.

Launching:

  • creates the ship in Shakedown status and starts its timeline;
  • makes your chosen officers its CO and XO;
  • sends them a COMPASS welcome email if they don't have an account yet;
  • tells the other regional officers who look after shakedown.

The new CO then imports the chapter's roster as usual. See Getting Started.

docs.title: Converting a chapter to shakedown
docs.text:
A chapter that joined COMPASS on its own is set to Deployed. If it's actually a chapter-in-training, convert it:

  1. Open the ship's Status page (from its Fleet Status card on the Regional Dashboard).
  2. Under Chapter-in-Training, click Convert to Chapter-in-Training.
  3. Set the Launch Date (it defaults to today), optionally a Support Ship, and a Reason.
  4. Tick the confirmation and click Convert to Chapter-in-Training.

The chapter keeps its crew, roles, registry and history. It gains the monthly START Manual checklist, a launch date and a support ship, and its commissioned date is cleared.

docs.title: Changing the launch date
docs.text:
The launch date drives which monthly checklist windows are open, and the minimum and target commission dates.

  1. On the chapter's shakedown page, click Change next to Launch.
  2. Pick the New Launch Date and give a Reason for Change.
  3. Click Save Launch Date.

Changing it shifts which checklist months are open. The old and new dates are recorded.

docs.title: Changing the support ship
docs.text:
1. On the chapter's shakedown page, click Change next to Support Ship.
  2. Choose the New Support Ship, or None / not in COMPASS.
  3. Give a Reason for Change and click Save Support Ship.

The same rules apply as at launch: only deployed chapters can be chosen, a cross-region support ship needs both RCs' approval, and COMPASS warns if the ship has been commissioned for less than 12 months — that needs a waiver from the RC and the Chief of ShOC.

docs.title: Commissioning a chapter
docs.text:
When a chapter-in-training has completed shakedown, open it on the Chapters-in-Training board and click Commission Ship.

The top of the page checks the essentials: Active Crew (10 required), Min Period (7 months — the ASP can't shorten it further), the Target Date, and the XO OCC.

  1. Enter the New Commission Registry in NCC-##### format. DTS must approve it.
  2. Work through Commission Requirements. Some are auto-verified by COMPASS (crew count, CO and XO OCC, the minimum period, monthly reporting); tick the rest yourself (DTS approval of the NCC registry, the commission VRR submitted to the region, and so on).
  3. Add any Commission Notes.
  4. Click Commission Ship and confirm.

The chapter becomes Deployed with its new NCC registry. This can't be undone.

Commissioning early

If the minimum 7-month shakedown period hasn't passed, COMPASS shows the earliest commission date. Commissioning before it needs a waiver from the RC and the Chief of ShOC.

docs.title: Operational status
docs.text:
Open a ship's Status page from its Fleet Status card on the Regional Dashboard.

Status Meaning Deployed Fully operational: meetings held regularly, events reported monthly. Stand-By Temporarily inactive. Keeps its membership but no active programming. Time-limited. Dry-Docked Like Stand-By, usually for maintenance or reorganisation. Restricted Under administrative review or probation. Activities or awards may be restricted. Reserve Reduced activity in low-membership or semi-active periods. Annual reporting still required. Decommissioned Formally closed.

To change it:

  1. Choose the New Status.
  2. Enter a Reason (at least 10 characters). It's recorded in the ship's Status History at the bottom of the page.
  3. Click Update Status.

Decommissioning

Decommissioning moves every active crew member to unassigned status, closes all ship and department assignments, and removes ship roles. Member records — rank, awards, academy, service history — are kept. It affects the whole crew and can't easily be undone.

Stand-By and Restricted chapters still count as operating and keep their Fleet Status card on the Regional Dashboard. Dry-Docked, Reserve and Decommissioned chapters move to Non-Operational Ships.

docs.title: Managing Unassigned Members
docs.text:
Unassigned members are STARFLEET members in your region who don't belong to a chapter. With no CO to look after them, the region does: you keep their records current, recognise them with awards, approve their promotions, and help them find a ship.

About the screenshots

The screenshots on this page come from a test copy of COMPASS. Names and SCCs are blurred.

docs.title: Who can do what
docs.text: Task Who See unassigned members RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO, RAO Import from db.sfi.org, edit details, update academy records RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO Nominate for an award RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO, RAO Approve promotions (Set Rank) RC, VRC Place a member on a ship (Direct Transfer) RC, VRC, RCOS, RCOO

docs.title: The dashboard
docs.text:
Go to Regional Dashboard → Regional Actions → Unassigned Members, or click Unassigned Members in the summary bar.

Card Meaning Total Unassigned Everyone on your region's unassigned list. Active Members Unassigned members with a current SFI membership. Inactive/Expired Members whose membership has lapsed. Needs Rank Members COMPASS has no rank for. Set one (see Setting a rank). Archived Members who have dropped off db.sfi.org's unassigned list (see Importing).

Management Actions link to the full list, importing, inactive members and regional reports. Recent Activity shows recently added members and recent imports.

Members waiting for a ship aren't listed

A member whose chapter isn't on COMPASS yet, or whose ship has withdrawn from COMPASS, is waiting for that ship rather than unassigned. They don't appear on this list or in its counts, and they're connected automatically if the ship joins.

docs.title: The member list
docs.text:
Click View All Members.

Filter by Status (active or inactive) or search by SCC or name. Each row shows the SCC, rank (UNRANKED if none), name, location, status, and membership expiration. Family members are marked Family of SCC ….

Each row has two shortcuts:

  • Assign — place the member on a ship straight away. See Direct Transfer.
  • Set Rank — record a rank or promotion.

Click a member's name to open their record, where you'll also find Edit Member, Academy Records, Nominate for Award and Promote.

docs.title: Keeping the list current
docs.text:
Unassigned members come from db.sfi.org's Region Unassigned Roster. Refresh it regularly.

Click Import Members on the dashboard or list. There are two ways to import:

docs.title: Pull live from SFI (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Click Pull Unassigned Roster from SFI.
  2. Sign in with your own db.sfi.org credentials. They're used for this pull only and aren't stored.

COMPASS reads the same report you'd see at db.sfi.org/region/unassigned.php. It adds new members and updates existing ones. Members who no longer appear on it — because they joined a chapter, for example — are archived out of the active list. Their record and history are kept.

docs.title: Paste a CSV
docs.text:
If the live pull isn't working, export the unassigned roster from db.sfi.org as CSV and paste it into the box. The page lists the columns it expects. COMPASS creates new members and updates existing ones by SCC.

After either import, the results page shows what was added, updated and skipped.

docs.title: Editing a member
docs.text:
On the member's record, click Edit Member to correct their first and last name, email, rank, phone, city or state.

Note

db.sfi.org is the official record. Your next import will update most of these details from SFI, so correct anything wrong on db.sfi.org too.

docs.title: Updating academy records
docs.text:
Unassigned members don't have a CO to keep their SFI Academy counts up to date.

  1. On the member's record, click Academy Records.
  2. Enter their Distinction, Honors and Pass totals — the cumulative counts from the SFI Academy.
  3. Click Update Records.

docs.title: Nominating for an award
docs.text:
1. On the member's record, click Nominate for Award.
  2. Choose the Award.
  3. Write the Citation, and add Supporting Evidence and Regional Notes if you have them.
  4. Click Submit Nomination.

With no ship and no CO, the nomination skips chapter review and goes straight to regional review — the RAO and RC. It then follows the normal regional process in Awards (RC). If the member already has this award, COMPASS warns you; tick Override duplicate-award check and give a reason if it's intentional.

docs.title: Setting a rank or approving a promotion
docs.text: Click Set Rank on the list, or Promote on the member's record. Unassigned members can also request a promotion themselves. Both are covered in Approving Unassigned Member Promotions.

docs.title: Placing a member on a ship
docs.text:
Members normally choose a ship themselves — see Joining or Changing Ships. When you need to place someone directly (for example, after a chapter closes), click Assign on the list:

  1. Choose the Destination Ship from the operating ships in the region.
  2. Optionally set a Rank, or keep their current one.
  3. Add a Reason and click Transfer Member.

A direct transfer takes effect immediately. Remind the member to update their chapter on db.sfi.org, or the next roster import will disagree.

docs.title: Approving Unassigned Member Promotions
docs.text:
Members who are not on a chapter roster in COMPASS — unassigned members — can request their own promotions. Under MHB Section 02:09 you may promote unassigned members up to O-6, so these requests come to you rather than to a CO.

This page walks through reviewing and approving one. For ship promotions and flag nominations, see Promotions (RC). For what the member sees, see Requesting a Promotion (Unassigned Members).

docs.title: How Requests Reach You
docs.text:
A member's request lands in O6 & Below Pending Approval on your Regional Promotions page. The section holds everything you approve directly — enlisted, cadet and junior officer requests from unassigned members as well as Captain promotions from ships.

You can tell a self-request at a glance:

  • Ship is Unassigned
  • Submitted By is the member themselves
  • From Rank may read Unranked for a member who has never held a rank
  • CO Recommendation is empty — unassigned members have no CO

Select Review on the row.

docs.title: Reviewing the Request
docs.text:
The review panel shows the member, the rank they are requesting, their points, the promotion date, and the supporting notes they wrote themselves. There is no CO recommendation section for a self-request.

COMPASS has already limited what the member could ask for: the next rank on their own track, no higher than O-6. An unranked member chooses their track with their first rank — CRMN 3C (Fleet), CRR (Fleet Reserve) or PVT (SFMC) — or CZN.

docs.title: Approving
docs.text:
Select Approve Promotion, add optional notes, and confirm with Approve Promotion.

The member's rank updates in COMPASS straight away and they are notified.

docs.title: Rejecting
docs.text: Select Reject Promotion and enter a reason (required). The request leaves your queue, and the member is notified by email and push notification with your reason — so write it for them to read.

docs.title: Recording It in the SFI Database
docs.text:
After approving, a Promotion Recorded prompt appears in the corner of the page:

  • Submit Directly sends the new rank to db.sfi.org for you.
  • Open Manually opens the member's rank page on db.sfi.org so you can enter it yourself.
  • Dismiss closes the prompt.

If you close the prompt without updating db.sfi.org, a reminder stays on your pages until you deal with it. The member is never asked to do this — it is your step.

docs.title: If Your Region Has No RC in COMPASS
docs.text: Requests from members in a region without an RC in COMPASS are emailed to the RC address the member enters (normally rc#@sfi.org). The email contains a secure review link where the RC can Approve or Reject without a COMPASS account. These requests appear under External RC Review on the Regional Promotions page so regional staff can see them.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
CO — Commanding Officer. The ship's captain and primary COMPASS administrator.

COMPASS — Crew Operations Management & Personnel Assignment Support System.

db.sfi.org — The SFI Members Portal. COMPASS supplements but does not replace it.

EC — Executive Committee. SFI's governing body at the fleet level.

LOA — Leave of Absence. A temporary inactive status for members who intend to return.

OCC — Officer Candidate Course. An academy track for officer advancement.

OTS — Officer Training School. Entry-level officer training tracked in permanent points.

Permanent Points — Cumulative point total driving promotion eligibility. Earned through events, awards, academy completions, and leadership positions.

RC — Regional Coordinator. The regional administrator responsible for a group of ships.

RCOS — Regional Chief of Staff. Assists the RC in regional operations.

SCC — Star Cluster Certification (member number). Unique identifier for every SFI member.

SFI — STARFLEET International. The fan organization COMPASS serves.

SFMC — Star Fleet Marine Corps. SFI's marine auxiliary, managed through a dedicated COMPASS module.

XO — Executive Officer. The ship's first officer; shares most CO permissions in COMPASS.

docs.title: Promotion Point System
docs.text:
This page documents the default point values COMPASS ships with. Every value here is a starting point — a chapter can override most of them, and some chapters turn point tracking off entirely.

Your chapter's numbers may differ

COMPASS is supplemental and voluntary. Promotion policy belongs to your Commanding Officer, not to COMPASS. If your chapter has published its own promotion point policy, that policy wins. This page tells you what COMPASS does when nobody has changed anything.

docs.title: The Two Point Pools
docs.text:
COMPASS tracks promotion points in two pools that behave differently.

Pool Made up of Behaviour Event + Academy Event participation, event point adjustments, academy completions Spent on promotions. Approving a promotion deducts its point cost from this pool. Awards + Permanent Award point values, permanent point awards Standing balance. Counts toward every eligibility check and is never consumed.

Eligibility compares (Event + Academy − already spent) + (Awards + Permanent) against the target rank's point cost.

Why the pools differ

Many chapters describe regular points as "resetting at each new rank." COMPASS implements the same idea by spending points rather than zeroing them, which keeps the full earning history intact for reports and audits. The available balance behaves the same way either way.

Event points are summed across a member's whole career, not per ship. A member who transfers carries both their earned points and their spent points to the new chapter, so the two sides stay coherent.

docs.title: Event Points
docs.text:
Each event type has a base value and a uniform multiplier applied when the member is recorded as having worn uniform.

Event Type Base Uniform Multiplier In Uniform Counts for Attendance Meeting or Event 2 ×2 4 Yes Games with Crewmates 2 ×2 4 Yes Fleet Challenges 2 ×1 2 No Plan or Host an Event 3 ×1 3 No Away Mission (individual or small group) 1 ×2 2 No Write an Article 2 ×1 2 No Attend a Convention 3 ×2 6 Yes Participating in a Charity Event 2 ×2 4 Yes Renewing Membership on Time 5 ×1 5 No Recruiting a Member 5 ×1 5 No Running the Chapter Table at a Convention 5 ×1 5 Yes Running a Convention Panel 5 ×1 5 No Participating in Community Service 2 ×2 4 Yes

The uniform bonus is a multiplier, not an addition. A multiplier of ×2 doubles the event's value when the member is recorded in uniform. A multiplier of ×1 means uniform wear makes no difference — that is how COMPASS marks the event types where being in uniform isn't applicable, such as renewing a membership or writing an article.

Each event type also has a uniform bonus enabled switch. Turning it off suppresses the multiplier entirely, so the event is worth its base value whether or not uniform was worn.

Counts for Attendance controls whether the event feeds the crew activity report. It has no effect on points.

Members can also receive host credit separately from attendance credit for the same event, so a member who plans, hosts, and attends is credited for both.

Chapters that joined COMPASS partway through their history can set an opening balance with Event Point Adjustments instead of back-entering years of events. Adjustments are folded into the member's event point total rather than shown separately.

docs.title: Academy Points
docs.text:
Completion Grade Default Distinction 2 Honors 1 Pass 1 Beta Tester 2 Course Created 2

Beta Tester and Course Created always match whatever Distinction is set to, including after an override.

docs.title: Award Points
docs.text:
Award point values are set per award, not per category. The defaults break down roughly as follows.

Award Group Typical Default SFI Individual Awards 1 to 5, most commonly 1 or 3 SFA (Academy) Awards 1 Annual Awards 2 to 3 SFMC 1, with achievement-tier awards at 2, 3, or 5 SF Medical, Sciences, Special Operations, Tactical, Petfleet 1

Repeatable awards are worth their point value each time earned.

When COMPASS looks up an award's value for a ship, it resolves in this order and stops at the first match:

  1. A ship-level override for that specific award
  2. A legacy ship-level override for that award
  3. A ship-level override for the award's whole category
  4. The award's own point value
  5. The system-wide default for the award's category

This is why a CO can say "all Medical awards are worth 1 point on my ship" with a single category override, without touching 53 individual awards.

docs.title: Permanent Points
docs.text:
Permanent points never reset and are never spent. Each category has a cap on the total a member can hold from that category.

Category Cap Academic Development Program 100 Auxiliary Special Award 60 Leadership Positions 75 Bridge Officer Certification 20 Officer Training No cap Other No cap

docs.title: Academic Development Program
docs.text: Award Points Associate Degree 10 Bachelor Degree 15 Masters Degree 25 Doctorate Degree 40 Additional Doctorate 30

docs.title: Auxiliary Special Award
docs.text:
Award Points Auxiliary Special Award 30

Covers recognitions such as the Black Ops Specialty Pin, the Specialist Medical Training Program, and SFMC achievement awards at silver or higher.

docs.title: Leadership Positions
docs.text:
Award Points Leadership Position (Chapter) 50 Leadership Position (Region) 75 Leadership Position (Fleet) 75

The 75-point category cap means a member holding both a chapter and a regional position is credited 75, not 125.

docs.title: Bridge Officer Certification
docs.text: Award Points Bridge Officer Certification 20

docs.title: Officer Training
docs.text: Award Points Officer Training School (OTS) 5 Officer Training School — Distinction 10 Officer Command Course (OCC) 15 Officer Command Course — Distinction 30

docs.title: Rank Costs and Time in Grade
docs.text: Point cost is what the promotion consumes; time in grade (TIG) is the minimum months a member must hold their current rank before becoming eligible.

docs.title: Navy Enlisted
docs.text:
Grade Rank Points TIG E-1 CRR / CRMN 3C — — E-2 CRA / CRMN 2C 20 1 E-3 CRMN / CRMN 1C 30 2 E-4 PO3 50 3 E-5 PO2 80 3 E-6 PO1 150 3 E-7 CPO 200 4 E-8 SCPO 250 5 E-9 MCPO 300 6

E-1 through E-3 run as two parallel tracks. A member on the reserve track (CRR → CRA → CRMN) is never offered the regular track (CRMN 3C → CRMN 2C → CRMN 1C), or the reverse. The tracks converge at E-4.

docs.title: Officer Prerequisites
docs.text:
Points and time in grade are not the only gate on officer ranks.

Target Requirement O-1 through O-4 Officer Training School (OTS or OTS Distinction) O-5 and above OTS and Officer Command Course (OCC or OCC Distinction)

A member at E-1 through E-5 who holds OTS also sees O-1 (ENS or 2LT) as a commissioning option alongside their normal next enlisted rank.

Enlisted and Warrant Officer promotions have no course prerequisites.

docs.title: Time in Grade Waivers
docs.text: A CO — or an officer they have delegated promotion authority to — can apply a TIG waiver at promotion time, which halves the time-in-grade requirement for that promotion. For Captain/Colonel and above, a waiver instead takes 6 months off the requirement. Waivers are intended for exceptional performance and are recorded on the promotion.

docs.title: Turning Points Off
docs.text:
Some chapters do not use a point system at all. Ship Settings has toggles for this.

Toggle Effect Promotion points disabled Master switch. All point totals report as zero and every rank costs 0. Event points disabled Event participation and adjustments stop counting. Academy points disabled Academy completions stop counting. Award points disabled Award values stop counting. Permanent points disabled Permanent point awards stop counting. TIG disabled All time-in-grade requirements become 0 months.

With points disabled, promotions become a pure Captain's Prerogative workflow — COMPASS still records the promotion, the rank change, and the notification.

docs.title: Where to Change These Values
docs.text:
Everything on this page is configured under Ship Settings:

  • Event Points — base value, uniform multiplier, and uniform bonus toggle per event type
  • Academy Points — Distinction, Honors, and Pass values
  • Award Points — per-award and per-category overrides
  • Permanent Award Points — permanent point values
  • Promotion Requirements — point cost and TIG per rank
  • Event Point Adjustments — opening balances and bulk corrections

See Ship Settings for the walkthrough.

Warning

Changing promotion requirements takes effect immediately and recalculates eligibility for your whole crew. Check the Promotion Eligibility Report afterwards to see what moved.
